[Verse 40]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

[Verse 41]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.
[Verse 44]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. The gathered warriors, eager for battle,

What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

[Verse 4-5]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

[Verse 8]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

[Verse 10]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

[Verse 11]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

शुद्ध - अशुद्ध, शत्रु-मित्र, दुष्ट - सज्जन, पापात्मा - पुण्यात्मा आदि जो कुछ भी देखने, सुनने, कहने, सोचने, समझने आदिमें
आता है, वह सब केवल भगवान् ही हैं। भगवान्‌ के सिवाय कहीं कुछ भी नहीं है।

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

[ अध्याय ७
हूँ और वे मेरेमें नहीं हैं'– ऐसा कहकर भगवान्ने यह भाव प्रकट किया है कि अगर कोई मनुष्य मेरेको सत्ता और महत्ता
न देकर सात्त्विक, राजस और तामस गुण, पदार्थ तथा क्रियाको सत्ता और महत्ता देकर उनके साथ सम्बन्ध जोड़ेगा
तो वह मेरेको प्राप्त न होकर जन्म-मरणमें चला जायगा – 'कारणं गुणसंगोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ' (गीता १३ । २१) ।
|
'मत्त एव' पदोंका प्रयोग करके भगवान् मानो यह कहते हैं कि तीनों गुण मेरेसे ही होते हैं, फिर तुम मेरी
तरफ न आकर गुणोंमें क्यों फँसते हो ? जो गुणोंमें फँस जाते हैं, वे मेरा भजन नहीं कर सकते (गीता - इसी अध्यायका
तेरहवाँ श्लोक)। परन्तु जो गुणोंमें नहीं फँसते, वे भक्त मेरा भजन करते हैं (गीता - सातवें अध्यायका सोलहवाँ और
दसवें अध्यायका आठवाँ श्लोक) । ये गुण टिकनेवाले नहीं हैं; क्योंकि कारण टिकता है, कार्य नहीं टिकता । जैसे
सोना टिकता है, गहने नहीं टिकते; मिट्टी टिकती है, घड़ा नहीं टिकता, ऐसे ही भगवान् टिकते हैं, गुण नहीं टिकते।
गुण तो परिवर्तनशील और मिटनेवाले हैं, पर भगवान् नित्य - निरन्तर ज्यों-के-त्यों रहनेवाले हैं । उनका न परिवर्तन
होता है, न नाश। इसलिये भगवान्‌की प्राप्ति गुणोंसे नहीं होती, प्रत्युत गुणोंके सम्बन्ध-विच्छेदसे होती है। अतः
तमोगुणको रजोगुणसे और रजोगुणको सत्त्वगुणसे जीतकर गुणोंसे अतीत होना है।
यहाँ एक विशेष बात समझनेयोग्य है कि सगुण-साकार भगवान् भी वास्तवमें निर्गुण ही हैं; क्योंकि वे सत्त्व,
रज और तमोगुणसे युक्त नहीं हैं, प्रत्युत ऐश्वर्य, माधुर्य, सौन्दर्य, औदार्य आदि गुणोंसे युक्त हैं। इसलिये सगुण-साकार
भगवान्‌की भक्तिको भी निर्गुण (सत्त्वादि गुणोंसे रहित) बताया गया है; जैसे- 'मन्निष्ठं निर्गुणं स्मृतम्', 'मन्निकेतं
तु निर्गुणम्', 'निर्गुणो मदपाश्रयः', 'मत्सेवायां तु निर्गुणा' (श्रीमद्भा० ११ । २५ । २४–२७)।
प्रश्न- -जब सब कुछ भगवान् ही हैं, तो फिर सात्त्विक - राजस - तामस भाव त्याज्य क्यों हैं ?
-
उत्तर—जैसे जमीनमें जल सब जगह रहता है, पर उसका प्राप्ति - स्थान कुआँ है, ऐसे ही भगवान् सब जगह
हैं, पर उनका प्राप्ति-स्थान यज्ञ ( कर्तव्य - कर्म ) है - ' तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ' ( गीता ३ । १५) ।
परन्तु सात्त्विक-राजस-तामस भाव भगवान् के प्राप्ति - स्थान नहीं हैं अर्थात् इनके द्वारा भगवान्‌की प्राप्ति नहीं होती
( गीता - इसी अध्यायका तेरहवाँ श्लोक) । अतः ये साधकके लिये कामके नहीं हैं। इसलिये भगवान्ने कहा है कि
ये भाव मेरेसे होनेपर भी मैं इनमें और ये मेरेमें नहीं हैं ।
जैसे, बाजरीकी खेतीमें बाजरी ही मुख्य होती है, पत्ती - डंठल नहीं । किसानका लक्ष्य केवल बाजरीको प्राप्त
करनेका ही होता है। बाजरीको प्राप्त करनेके लिये वह खेतीको जल, खाद आदिसे पुष्ट करता है, जिससे बढ़िया
बाजरी प्राप्त हो सके। ऐसे ही साधकका लक्ष्य भी केवल भगवान्‌का होना चाहिये, संसारका नहीं । भगवान्‌को प्राप्त
करनेके लिये साधकको संसारकी सेवा करनी चाहिये । सेवाके सिवाय संसारसे अपना कोई मतलब नहीं रखना चाहिये ।
महत्त्व बाजरी (दाने-) का है, पत्ती - डंठलका नहीं; क्योंकि आरम्भमें भी बाजरी रहती है और अन्तमें भी बाजरी
ही रहती है। बाजरी प्राप्त करनेके बाद जो शेष बचता है, वह (पत्ती - डंठल ) बाजरीसे अलग न होनेपर भी अपने
लिये किसी कामकी चीज नहीं है, प्रत्युत पशुओंके खानेकी चीज है। ऐसे ही सात्त्विक - राजस - तामस भाव मूढ़
(अविवेकी) मनुष्योंके लिये हैं । ये तीनों ही भाव मनुष्यको बाँधनेवाले हैं (गीता-चौदहवें अध्यायका पाँचवाँ श्लोक) ।
इसलिये ये भाव भगवान् के रूप होते हुए भी स्वयंके लिये नहीं हैं, प्रत्युत विवेकपूर्वक सांसारिक व्यवहारके लिये
हैं । जैसे, जहर भी भगवान्‌का रूप है, पर वह खानेके लिये नहीं है !
जैसे बाजरी (बीज) - से पत्ती - डंठल पैदा होनेपर भी पत्ती - डंठलमें बाजरी नहीं है और बाजरीमें पत्ती- डंठल
नहीं है, ऐसे ही भगवान् से पैदा होनेपर भी सात्त्विक - राजस - तामस भावोंमें भगवान् नहीं हैं और भगवान्में सात्त्विक-
राजस - तामस भाव नहीं हैं।

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.
[Verse 16]

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

[ Verse 16 ]
* Sadhak Sanjivani *
The Lord has dedicated everything to the devotee and has no desire to receive anything from the devotee. The Lord has not kept any possibility of receiving anything from the devotee. Therefore, the Lord is called 'Udarah' (7.18). The Lord alone truly loves. The devotee needs the Lord, so the devotee feels a sense of belonging to the Lord. When the devotee dedicates himself completely to the Lord without any desire to receive anything, he is called a wise devotee, a loving devotee. By dedicating himself completely to the Lord, the devotee's existence is not separate from the Lord, but rather the Lord's existence alone remains. Special Topic
(1)
Four boys were playing. Their father came with four mangoes. One boy started asking for a mango, and another boy started crying for a mango. The father gave each of them a mango. The third boy did not ask or cry, but just looked at the mango. The fourth boy did not even look at the mango and continued playing. The boy who asked for the mango is like the devotee who seeks material gain (Artharthi), the boy who cried is like the devotee who is distressed (Arta), the boy who looked at the mango is like the devotee who is curious (Jijnasu), and the boy who did not look at the mango is like the wise devotee (Jnani). Similarly, the devotee who seeks material gain asks the Lord for favors, the distressed devotee asks the Lord to remove his troubles, the curious devotee wants to know the Lord, and the wise devotee does not want anything from the Lord. The devotees who seek material gain, who are distressed, who are curious, and who are wise - all four are devoted to the Lord. Therefore, they cannot be considered as those who have fallen from yoga (Gita - 6th chapter, 41st-42nd verses). Similarly, the devotees who seek material gain and who are distressed are different from those who are driven by desires, because these two types of devotees have the Lord as their primary refuge. The person driven by desires is always focused on fulfilling his desires and is therefore considered to be without knowledge (Gita 7.20), and is thus considered to be a person with demonic tendencies. Although there may be some differences among the devotees who seek material gain, who are distressed, who are curious, and who are wise, due to the presence of desires, the fact that they take refuge in the Lord is the primary factor. As their devotion to the Lord deepens, their desire-driven nature decreases, and their uniqueness increases. Therefore, the Lord calls them 'Udarah' (7.18) and considers the wise devotee to be His own self - 'Jnani tvatmaiv me matam' (7.18). (2)
There is no other means, no other yoga, no other strength, and no other qualification equal to feeling a sense of belonging to the Lord. The Lord's sense of belonging to all living beings has always been and will always be. It is the living being who has forgotten this sense of belonging and has instead developed a sense of belonging to the world. Therefore, this mistaken sense of belonging must be removed, and the inherent sense of belonging to the Lord must be recognized. To recognize the Lord as one's own, one does not need the help of the mind, intellect, or anything else, whereas other means require the help of the mind, intellect, and so on. When the devotee feels a sense of belonging to the Lord, that is, when he firmly believes "I am only the Lord's and the Lord is only mine," he may still see shortcomings in his own heart, but these shortcomings will not persist. Moreover, even if the devotee has some shortcomings, the Lord's gaze is only on the sense of belonging, not on the shortcomings. This is because the sense of belonging we have with the Lord is real. The Lord's sense of belonging is the same even for the most wicked person. Therefore, in the 16th chapter, while describing those with demonic tendencies, the Lord says, "I cast the cruel, hateful, and wicked into demonic wombs." In this way, the Lord purifies them by casting them into demonic wombs. Just as a mother bathes her child without seeking the child's consent, the Lord purifies them without seeking their consent, because the Lord has a sense of belonging to them.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

Dhritarashtra said:
1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

Maharshi Vedavyasa had a lot of affection for Dhritarashtra. Due to this affection, he went to Dhritarashtra and said, "War is inevitable and a great massacre of warriors is certain. This cannot be avoided. If you want to see the war, I can give you divine vision, so that you can see the war clearly sitting here." Dhritarashtra replied, "I have been blind since birth, I do not want to see the destroyers of my family, but I want to know how the war is happening - I want to hear the news of it." Then Vedavyasa said, "I will give divine vision to Sanjaya, so that he can see the entire war, all the events, the thoughts of the warriors, and he will tell you everything."

As per the fixed time, the war started in Kurukshetra. Sanjaya stayed at the war site for ten days. When grandfather Bhishma was thrown off his chariot by arrows, Sanjaya went to Hastinapura (where Dhritarashtra was sitting) and told him this news. After hearing this news, Dhritarashtra was very sad and started crying. Then he asked Sanjaya to tell him the entire story of the war. In the beginning of the 25th chapter of the Bhishma Parva, Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya-

Dhritarashtra said:
In the field of dharma, in Kurukshetra,
The gathered warriors, eager for battle,
My sons, the Pandavas, and the Kauravas too,
What were they doing, Sanjaya? 1

1. In the Mahabharata, there are eighteen parvas. Among them, this 'Shrimad Bhagavad Gita Parva' is a part of the Bhishma Parva, starting from the 13th chapter and ending at the 42nd chapter. 2. The conversation between Vaisampayana and Janamejaya is 'Dhritarashtra - Sanjaya - Sambandh', and the conversation between Dhritarashtra and Sanjaya is 'Shri Krishna Arjuna - Sambandh'. 3. Sanjaya was born from Gavalgana, a Suta. He was a wise and righteous person, like a sage - 'Sanjayo munikalpa stu jajneya sutah gavalganaat' (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 63.97). He was Dhritarashtra's minister.

सत्-ही-सत् है, असत् है ही नहीं । वासुदेव - ही - वासुदेव है, 'सर्वम्' है ही नहीं । परन्तु कहने, सुनने, पढ़नेवाले साधकोंकी

कर्मयोगी, ज्ञानयोगी, ध्यानयोगी, लययोगी, हठयोगी, राजयोगी, मन्त्रयोगी, अनासक्तयोगी आदि अनेक तरहके

ही है' – इसका अनुभव करनेवाले महात्माको ही अत्यन्त दुर्लभ बताते हैं ।
-
