* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18
The Lord takes one to Himself. In action, two become two, and in love, two become one, i.e., the sense of duality never disappears, never disappears. *

Parishishta Bhaav – In the previous shloka, the attainment of the eternal state was described, and now the method of attaining it is being explained. For the sadhak, there are only two special tasks - renunciation of the world's relationship and the relationship with the Lord (love). In the previous shloka, the emphasis was on the relationship with the Lord in the phrase 'madvyapashaayaH', and in this shloka, the emphasis is on the renunciation of the world's relationship in the phrase 'buddhiyogamupaashritya'. The meaning of 'buddhiyogamupaashritya' is that there should be no subtle relationship with the world - 'dureNa hy avaram karma buddhiyogAdhAnanjaya' (Gita 2.49), there should be no trace of attachment or aversion towards anyone. By constantly thinking of the Lord alone, equanimity (buddhiyog) arises automatically, hence it is said, 'maccittah satatam bhava'. The relationship - In the previous shloka, the command was given, and now the Lord will confirm it in the next two shlokas, respectively, with anuvart and vyatireka. Hence, you will overcome all obstacles by My grace. And if you think, "I am superior to you," you will not hear Me, and you will perish. 58. *

Explanation - 'maccittah tatarishyasi' - The Lord says that by being devoted to Me, you will overcome all obstacles, troubles, sorrows, and sufferings with My grace, i.e., you will not have to make any effort to overcome them. The entire responsibility of removing obstacles, troubles, and sorrows will be on Me. Therefore, the Lord says, 'matprasadaat tatarishyasi', i.e., you will overcome all obstacles by My grace. This means that the devotee will do what he can, and what he cannot do, will be taken care of by the Lord's grace. The devotee will do his part with full caution, and what is lacking will be fulfilled by the Lord's grace. The devotee will surrender all his actions to the Lord, and he will become one with the Lord. He will become detached from the world's relationships, and he will be established in the Lord's relationship. Even then, if there is any deficiency or if there is any subtle defect, it will be removed by the Lord's grace. The devotee will not have to worry about it. The devotee's only task is to surrender to the Lord and to be devoted to Him. The Lord will take care of the rest. The meaning of 'bodhe praga jate bodhe manisha' is that the duality that arises before the awakening of knowledge can lead to delusion. However, the duality that arises after the awakening of knowledge is accepted for the sake of devotion and is even more beautiful than non-duality. The ultimate truth is non-duality, but for the sake of devotion, duality is accepted. If such devotion is there, it is even more valuable than liberation.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

It is not visible, but it appears in the form of mercy. 1.209
That is, only a slight mercy is visible in the world to attain the mercy of God. Therefore, considering it as an obstacle in the form of obstacles and becoming distant from God - this was the only obstacle. He removed that obstacle, and now God's mercy will bring complete attainment on its own. The nature and activities of nature, which are related to the body and its parts, are subject to the rules and prohibitions of the scriptures, and the observance of duties according to one's varna and ashrama. This is because good and evil deeds, and their fruits, happiness and suffering, are all related to the body and its parts. Therefore, the scriptural norms and rules are especially applicable to it. But he who is completely detached from nature and its activities, and stands before God, is not bound by scriptural rules and prohibitions, nor by the norms of varna and ashrama. He transcends the rules and prohibitions, because the rules and prohibitions are mainly applicable in the kingdom of nature. In the kingdom of God, it is devotion that is paramount. There is a possibility of obstacles and hindrances in the path of spiritual practice, and also the possibility of obstacles in attaining God. For this reason, God says that I will do both of your tasks, that is, I will remove all the obstacles and hindrances in your path of spiritual practice, and also attain God through that practice. 'If you do not listen to my words, you will perish' - God is saying this to Arjuna with great compassion, as if speaking to a dear friend. 'If you do not listen to my words, you will perish' - this means that if you do not listen to my words due to ignorance or due to some mistake, it is pardonable; but if you do not listen to my words due to pride, then your downfall is certain, because pride is the root of all demonic qualities. The jiva is the direct part of the Supreme Being (Gita 15.7). If it moves only towards its own part, the Supreme Being, then there is no debt to be repaid to the gods, sages, living beings, mothers and fathers, and ancestors, because the pure consciousness has never taken anything from them. It is only when it associates itself with the body that debt arises; and debt arises only when there is a lack. Therefore, God himself has said in the fourth chapter that you are my devotee and dear friend, and that there is no lack in you - 'You are my devotee, you are my dear friend' (4.3). And in the second chapter, he has said that you are my devotee, and that there is no lack in you - 'You are my devotee, you are my dear friend' (2.16). If there is no lack in you, then how can you be a debtor to me? This is the complete downfall of my devotee - 'The devotee perishes' (9.31). This proves that in the path of spiritual practice, many obstacles and hindrances arise, such as the problem of earning a living, diseases in the body, and so on; but these obstacles and hindrances cannot arise, and the devotee's downfall cannot occur, because of the support of God's mercy. Arjuna, the devotee of God, will not be distracted by these obstacles and hindrances, but if he does not listen to God's words, he will become distant from God and will be overcome by these obstacles and hindrances. He will be overcome by these obstacles and hindrances because he will not have the support of God's mercy. As it is said in the eleventh chapter of the Bhagavatam, 'O king! He who, having renounced all actions, takes refuge in the Lord, the protector of the universe, and the Lord of the universe, is not a servant of anyone, nor is he a debtor to anyone' (11.5.41).

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

[ Chapter 18 ]

The meaning of this is that the ultimate goal is to be detached from worldly attachments. The reason for the downfall of living beings is that they are detached from God. In other words, they are trapped in the cycle of birth and death (Gita—9th chapter, 16th verse, and 20th verse). Special Note:

In the 11th verse of the 10th chapter, God said, "I manifest knowledge in the hearts of my devotees through my mercy." In the 38th verse of the 11th chapter, God said, "I have shown my divine form to you through my mercy." In the same chapter, 51st verse, God says, "Through my mercy, you will attain the ultimate goal" and "Through my mercy, you will overcome all obstacles."

The meaning of this is that God's mercy is the only means to attain the ultimate goal. Arjuna was afraid of fighting the war, thinking that it would lead to his downfall and the downfall of his family. He thought that if he surrendered to the enemy, it would be beneficial for him. However, God says that through his mercy, Arjuna will overcome all obstacles and attain the ultimate goal. In the 51st verse of this chapter, God says, "Through my mercy, you will overcome all obstacles." The use of the word "sarva" (all) with "durgani" (obstacles) implies that there will be no trace of sin in you, and you will be completely free from all bondages. In the same verse, God says, "You will attain the ultimate goal through my mercy." This implies that through God's mercy, one can attain the ultimate goal without any obstacles. The meaning of this is that God's mercy is the only means to attain the ultimate goal. It is not that one should not perform any actions, but rather, one should perform actions as a means to attain the ultimate goal. As it is said in the 16th verse of the 8th chapter, "If one does not attain God in this human birth, even if one goes to the highest realms, one will have to return to the cycle of birth and death."

Therefore, when one has obtained a human birth, one should strive to attain God in this life itself and become free from the cycle of birth and death. Even for the karma yogi, God says that a person who is equipoised in all circumstances becomes free from both good and bad karma (Gita—2nd chapter, 50th verse). The meaning of this is that becoming free from karma bondage is the ultimate goal of human life. Parishishta Bhaav:

The duty of a devotee is to take shelter in God and to think of God alone. Then, God Himself performs all his duties. God showers his special mercy on the devotee and removes all obstacles in his path to devotion. As it is said in the 22nd verse of the 9th chapter, "I will take care of your welfare and your livelihood." Therefore, it is said in the Brahma Sutras that "The special mercy of God is obtained through devotion" (3.4.38). In reality, God's mercy is always upon human beings, but through devotion, the devotee experiences this mercy.

The one who is determined by nature and has a fixed resolve, in him the predominance of the internal organ remains. Therefore, the Lord says to Arjuna, "You are saying that you will not fight, taking the shelter of your ego, which is the nature, this resolve of yours is false, it is a lie. * Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

[ Chapter 18 ]
[ Verse 60 ]

O, son of Kunti! You are bound by your own nature (svabhava) due to your own nature (svabhava). You do not want to do (karman) the actions (karma) that are bound by your own nature (svabhava). Explanation: 'svabhava-jen kaunteya nibaddhah svena karmana' -
The tendencies of actions and qualities that existed in your past life, the upbringing you received from your parents, the education you received, and the actions you performed - all these have created a habit in you, which is called svabhava. The Lord has called it svabhava-janya svakia karma. This is also known as svadharma - 'svadharma-apic cha avekshya na vikampitum arhasi' (Gita 2.31). 'Kartum naichchhasi yan mohat karsyasyavashoapi tat'
You will do (karishyasi) what you do not want to do (kartum naichchhasi) due to your attachment (mohat), even if you are forced (avashah). The scriptures have given the order to follow one's duty according to one's nature (svabhava). Even if there are shortcomings or defects in one's own actions, they are not considered to be obstacles (papa-janak). 'Shreyan svadharma vigunah paradharmaat svanushtitatah' (Gita 3.35; 18.47). You will be forced to fight (yuddh karne ke liye parvash hokar) according to your svabhava-janya karma (kshatriya-dharma). Your idea of not fighting (yuddh na karna) is foolish. You will also do (karishyasi) that (tat) due to your attachment (mohat) to your nature (svabhava-janya kshatriya-prakriti). That action (karman) will be beneficial for you. Because the attachment (raga-dvesha) to actions (karma) will be removed when you perform actions (karma) according to the scriptures or my order. Your vision will be towards the order (ajnaki taraf), not towards attachment (raga-dveshaki taraf). Therefore, those actions (karma) will not be binding (bandhan-karak), but will be beneficial (kalyan-karak). Special point
The idea of being controlled by nature (prakriti) is mentioned in the Gita in general (e.g. 3.33, 18.59). However, it is mentioned in two places in a special way - 'Prakritim yaanti bhutani' (3.33) and 'Prakritistvan niyokshyati' (18.59). This proves the power of nature (svabhava). Because any living being, in any birth, has its nature (prakriti) with it. If its nature (svabhava) is completely pure, then why is it born? If it is born, then its nature (svabhava) will be predominant - 'Karanam gunasango'sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu' (Gita 13.21). If its nature (svabhava) is predominant, and every action is according to its nature (svabhava), then what will be the effect of the scriptures' order (vidhi-nished)? What will be the effect of the guru's teaching (shiksha)? And how will a man (manushya) give up bad qualities (durgun-durachar) and adopt good qualities (sadgun-sadachar)? The nature (svabhava) of a liberated person (jivan-mukta mahapurush) is completely pure. Therefore, they are not controlled by their nature (svabhava). However, when they are engaged in any activity, they do it according to their nature (svabhava). But ordinary men (sadharn manushya) are controlled by their nature (prakriti), so their nature (svabhava) forces them to do actions (karma) against their will (Gita 3.33). The Lord says to Arjuna that your kshatriya-svabhava will also force you to fight (yuddh mein lagada dega), but its result will not be good for you. If you perform the action of fighting (yuddh-rup karma) according to the scriptures or the order of the saints (sant-mahapurush), or my order, then it can be purified (param shuddh, nirmal ban sakta hai). The meaning is that just as a man cannot stop the flow of the Ganges, but can divert it, similarly a man cannot give up his varna-uchit svabhava, but can make it free from attachment (raga-dvesh) by keeping the goal of attaining the Lord in mind. In the knowledge-yoga, a jnani (knowledgeable person) separates himself from his nature (prakriti), so the idea of being controlled by nature (prakriti) does not apply to him.

*
Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]
A person, being completely dependent on God, and being in His shelter, becomes free, not weak, and not a slave. Weakness and slavery are perceived only due to attachment and aversion. Now, for the purification of this nature, God has explained two methods in the Gita - Karma Yoga and Bhakti Yoga - (1) Karma Yoga: In the thirty-fourth verse of the third chapter, God has said that a person's special enemy is attachment and aversion. Therefore, one should not be under the control of attachment and aversion, i.e., one should not perform any action with attachment and aversion, but rather, one should perform every action according to the command of the scriptures. A person performs all actions with pleasure, following the command of the scriptures, the disciple follows the command of the guru, the son follows the command of the mother and father, the wife follows the command of the husband, and the servant follows the command of the master. In this way, there is no attachment and aversion in him. Because, by performing actions according to one's own will, attachment and aversion become strong. By performing actions according to the command of the scriptures, one's nature becomes pure (Gita - third chapter, thirty-fourth verse) and according to Bhakti Yoga, by being completely devoted to God, one's nature becomes pure (Gita - eighteenth chapter, sixty-first verse). When nature becomes pure, there is no question of bondage. A person performs all actions either under the control of attachment and aversion or according to the principles of the scriptures. By performing actions under the control of attachment and aversion, attachment and aversion become strong, and a person's nature becomes like that. By performing actions according to the principles of the scriptures, a person's nature becomes according to the principles of the scriptures. A person who performs actions with the intention of attaining the ultimate goal of life, following the principles of the scriptures and the great personalities, and a person who has already attained the ultimate goal of life - both their actions are a model for the world, worthy of imitation (Gita - third chapter, twenty-first verse). (2) According to Bhakti Yoga: When a person has a dual nature, consisting of a natural tendency to perform prescribed actions and a natural tendency to perform prohibited actions, the natural tendency to perform prescribed actions is a 'swabhava' (natural tendency) and the natural tendency to perform prohibited actions is a 'parabhava' (acquired tendency). The natural tendency to perform prescribed actions is a 'swa-svabhava' (natural tendency) because it is inherent, but the natural tendency to perform prohibited actions is a 'par-svabhava' (acquired tendency) because it is acquired. The natural tendency to perform prescribed actions is a 'sajatiya' (similar) tendency because it is inherent, but the natural tendency to perform prohibited actions is a 'vijatiya' (dissimilar) tendency because it is acquired. A person's special duty is to correct his nature, i.e., to give up the natural tendency to perform prohibited actions and to perform actions according to the natural tendency to perform prescribed actions. God has commanded to perform actions according to the natural tendency to perform prescribed actions. God says, "Whether you fight with the intention of duty alone or according to My command, you will have to fight. If you do not take My shelter, your ego will remain, and even prescribed actions will become binding. But if you take My shelter, your ego will not remain. Ego is the one that binds. A person who is not under the control of nature, whose nature is great and pure, even when he performs actions according to nature, how can a person whose nature is impure and under the control of nature perform actions contrary to nature? Relation: A living being is a part of God, and nature is a part of God; a living being is self-existent, and nature is created; a living being is conscious, and nature is unconscious - despite this, how does a living being become under the control of nature? In answer to this question, God says in the next verse:

The Lord is present in the heart of all beings, Arjuna, and is causing all beings to revolve like a puppet on a string, by His Maya. 61.

mayaya' – This means that the Lord, who is the ruler, regulator, and sustainer of all beings, and who is independent of all, operates these beings through His power, who have considered their body as 'I' and 'mine'. Just as an electrically operated machine, like a train, is controlled by the electric current, and when it is on the train, it has to follow the train's rules, but when it is not on the train, it does not follow the train's rules, similarly, as long as a person identifies with their body as 'I' and 'mine', the Lord operates them according to their nature, and they continue to be bound by the cycle of birth and death. The attachment to the body as 'I' and 'mine' gives rise to attachment and aversion, which makes the nature impure. When the nature is impure, the person becomes a slave to their nature. However, when the attachment to the body as 'I' and 'mine' is severed, the nature becomes pure, and the person is no longer a slave to their nature. When the nature is pure, the Lord's Maya does not operate on the person. Now, the question arises, if the Lord is operating us, then what is the freedom to act or not to act? Because we have become slaves to the body and the Lord, who is the operator, then why should we not follow His will? The answer is that just as an electric current operates a machine according to its nature, similarly, the Lord operates living beings according to their nature. Just as a machine, like a refrigerator, may have ice forming in it, and another machine, like a stove, may have fire burning in it, both machines are operated by the same electric current, but they perform opposite functions. However, the electric current does not have a preference for either ice or fire; it operates the machines according to their nature. Similarly, the Lord operates all living beings, including humans, animals, birds, gods, and demons, according to their nature. The implication is that the living beings, who identify themselves with their body as 'I' and 'mine', perform actions according to their nature. Good actions are performed by good-natured people, and bad actions are performed by bad-natured people. Therefore, the Lord's hand is not involved in good or bad actions; it is the hand of their own good or bad nature. Just as an electric current operates a machine according to its nature, similarly, the Lord operates living beings according to their nature. The nature of a living being is determined by their subtle and gross bodies. The subtle body is the cause of the gross body, and the gross body is the manifestation of the subtle body.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

[ Chapter 18 ]

The human being himself is the cause of his own downfall by misusing his nature. This will lead to dualism. The solution to this is that the Supreme Being, God, resides in the hearts of all living beings. This means that just as water is present everywhere on earth, but one can only access it from a well, similarly, God is present everywhere, but one can only access Him through one's heart. The heart is the abode of God, who is omnipresent. In the third chapter, it is said that God, who is omnipresent, is established in the ritual of selfless action, 'tasmat sarvagatam brahma nityam yajnesh pratishtitam' (Gita 3.15). Special Note

The seeker often commits a mistake by thinking that even though he is performing devotion, prayer, meditation, etc., God is still far away and will not be attained. He thinks that he is not worthy, that God's grace is not upon him, etc. This strengthens his belief in the separation from God. However, the seeker should be cautious and remember that since God is present in all living beings, He is also present in him. He should realize that God is omnipresent and is present in every breath, every thought, and every action. The 'I' (ahankara) that he thinks is separate from God is actually a part of God. When he recognizes this, he should perform devotion, prayer, and meditation with the understanding that God is present in him. When the seeker recognizes God as a part of himself, he does not experience duality, but rather, he experiences unity. This is because when he recognizes God as a part of himself, he experiences love and devotion. Just as the water in a well becomes polluted when it is separated from the Ganges River, but becomes pure again when it is reunited with the Ganges, similarly, when the seeker recognizes God as a part of himself, he experiences purification and becomes free from all vices. However, the seeker often has a doubt that when he recognizes God as a part of himself, he becomes two separate entities - the individual and God. This is a misconception. The fact is that the universe is controlled by God's power, 'mattoh sarvam pravartate' (Gita 10.8). God inspires living beings to perform their actions according to their nature, but He does not have any personal interest in their actions. It is because of this that living beings are influenced by their desires, attachments, and ego, and they perform good or bad actions, and suffer the consequences in the next life. However, when a person seeks refuge in God, God inspires him to perform actions that are in accordance with His will. Without ego, the person performs actions that are in accordance with God's inspiration. Connection

Now, God will explain the way to overcome the influence of the ego and the vices that arise from it. Tam eva sharanam gachcha sarvabhaavena bharat. Tatprasadaat paraam shaantim sthaanam prapsyasi shaashwatam. 62.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

[ Verse 62 ]

O descendant of the Bharata dynasty,
= O Arjuna! Take refuge in that all-pervading Lord,
= that all-pervading Lord,
who resides in the hearts of all beings
and is the controller of all. Go to Him,
= go to Him. Through His grace,
= through His grace,
you will attain the supreme and eternal abode,
= the supreme and eternal abode,
and attain the highest peace,
= the highest peace,
which is free from all worldly attachments. Commentary:

- It is a common weakness of human beings that even when saints and great souls are present before them, they do not have faith and reverence for them, nor do they consider them to be of great importance. However, when these saints and great souls leave, they begin to weep and repent. Similarly, the horses that pull Arjuna's chariot are harnessed and controlled by him, and they obey his commands. In the same way, when the Lord says to Arjuna, "Take refuge in Me, and through My grace, you will attain the supreme and eternal abode, and attain the highest peace, which is free from all worldly attachments," Arjuna does not say anything. This may also indicate that Arjuna did not have complete faith in the Lord's words. Therefore, the Lord is telling Arjuna to take refuge in the all-pervading Lord, who resides in the hearts of all beings and is the controller of all. 'tam eva sharanam gachcha' - The Lord says, "Take refuge in that all-pervading Lord, who resides in the hearts of all beings and is the controller of all." The meaning is that one should not take refuge in any worldly object, person, or thing that is subject to birth and death. Rather, one should take refuge only in the all-pervading Lord, who is beyond birth and death. The Lord had previously said that through His grace, one attains the supreme and eternal abode (shloka 50), and through His grace, one crosses over all obstacles (shloka 28). Now, He is saying the same thing, that through the grace of the all-pervading Lord, one attains the supreme and eternal abode, and attains the highest peace, which is free from all worldly attachments. In the Gita, the supreme and eternal abode is referred to as 'para shanti'. However, in this verse, the Lord uses both 'para shanti' and 'shashvat sthan' (supreme abode) together. Therefore, 'para shanti' should be understood as freedom from all worldly attachments, and 'shashvat sthan' should be understood as attaining the supreme abode. The Lord says, "Take refuge in that all-pervading Lord, who resides in the hearts of all beings and is the controller of all." This may raise the question, "Is the Lord Shri Krishna not the all-pervading Lord?" If He were the all-pervading Lord, then He would not have said, "Take refuge in Him" in a subtle way. The answer to this question is that the Lord has referred to the devotee of the all-pervading Lord as 'guhyatad guhyatar' (18.63), meaning the most secret of the secret. However, He has referred to His own devotee as 'sarva guhyatam' (18.64), meaning the most secret of all. This shows that the Lord Shri Krishna is greater than the all-pervading Lord. 'sarvabhaven' - The meaning of 'sarvabhaven' is that one should think of the all-pervading Lord in one's mind, worship Him through physical actions, and love Him with devotion. One should be pleased with His will and be satisfied with His actions. The Lord had previously said that one should be pleased with His will and be satisfied with His actions. 'atiparichayad avajnya' - When one has a great deal of familiarity with someone, one tends to be disrespectful towards them.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

[ Chapter 18 ]

The Lord manifests Himself through His Yoga Maya (the divine power of Yoga) (as mentioned in the fourth shloka of this chapter); I am the consumer of all Yajnas (sacrifices) and Taps (austerities), the great Lord of all the worlds, and the well-wisher of all living beings - by accepting this, one attains peace (as mentioned in the thirty-first shloka of the fifth chapter); but those who do not consider Me as the consumer of all Yajnas and the Lord of all, their downfall occurs (as mentioned in the twenty-fourth shloka of the ninth chapter). In this way, the Lord's divinity is also established through the principles of anumana (inference) and vyatireka (negation). In this chapter, it is said in the sixty-first shloka, "Ishwarah sarvabhootanam hrd-desh-e' rjuna tisthati" (18.61), that the Lord, who is the inner dweller, resides in the hearts of all beings, and in the fifteenth chapter, it is said in the fifteenth shloka, "Sarvasya chaaham hrdi sannivishtah" (15.15), that I am present in the hearts of all. The implication of this is that the inner dweller, the Supreme Being, and Lord Krishna are not two, but one. It was said that the attainment of this knowledge would be possible, and in the seventy-eighth and eighty-eighth shlokas, Arjuna was given the order to surrender to the Lord, saying, "You will be able to cross over all obstacles with My grace." However, Arjuna did not say anything, which means he did not accept anything. Therefore, the Lord threatened Arjuna, saying that if he did not listen to Him due to pride, he would suffer a downfall. In the seventy-sixth and eightieth shlokas, it was said, "I will not fight," and thus, taking refuge in pride, Arjuna's decision would not be firm, and he would be forced to fight due to his inherent nature. Even after the Lord said all this, Arjuna did not say anything. Therefore, in the end, the Lord had to say to Arjuna, "If you do not want to take refuge in Me, then go to the Lord who resides in the hearts of all beings, the inner dweller, the Supreme Being."

In reality, the inner dweller, the Supreme Being, and Lord Krishna are completely non-dual, meaning they are present in the hearts of all beings in the form of the inner dweller. Therefore, why did Lord Krishna say to Arjuna, "Go to the Lord who resides in the hearts of all beings, the inner dweller, the Supreme Being"? The reason for this is that the inner dweller, the Supreme Being, is present in the hearts of all beings, and the Lord is the same. Parishishta Bhaav - The jiva (the individual soul) is a part of the Lord, and therefore, the Lord says to take refuge in the Lord's shelter. Taking refuge in the Lord's shelter means there is no pride. As long as the jiva is not in the Lord's shelter, it remains under the control of nature. The more the jiva moves towards the material world, the more it acquires the qualities of the asuric (demonic) nature, and the more it moves towards the spiritual world, the more it acquires the qualities of the divine nature. Sambandh - In the previous shloka, the Lord told Arjuna to go to the Lord who resides in the hearts of all beings. Even after saying this, Arjuna did not say anything. Therefore, in the next shloka, the Lord gives Arjuna the freedom to think and act as he pleases. Iti te jnanam akhyatam guhyad guhyataram maya |

* साधक-संजीवनी *
'विमृश्यैतदशेषेण' – गुह्य - से - गुह्यतर शरणागतिरूप
ज्ञान बताकर भगवान् अर्जुनसे कहते हैं कि मैंने पहले
जो भक्तिकी बातें कही हैं, उनपर तुम अच्छी तरहसे विचार
कर लेना। भगवान्ने इसी अध्यायके सत्तावनवें - अट्ठावनवें
श्लोकोंमें अपनी भक्ति - (शरणागति - ) की जो बातें कही हैं,
उन्हें 'एतत्' पदसे लेना चाहिये । गीतामें जहाँ-जहाँ भक्तिकी
बातें आयी हैं, उन्हें 'अशेषेण' पदसे लेना चाहिये ।
'विमृश्यैतदशेषेण' कहनेमें भगवान्‌की अत्यधिक
कृपालुताकी एक गूढाभिसन्धि है कि कहीं अर्जुन मेरेसे विमुख
न हो जाय, इसलिये यदि यह मेरी कही हुई बातोंकी तरफ
विशेषतासे खयाल करेगा तो असली बात अवश्य ही इसकी
१२१९
समझमें आ जायगी और फिर यह मेरेसे विमुख नहीं होगा ।
'यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु' - पहले कही सब बातोंपर
पूरा-पूरा विचार करके फिर तेरी जैसी मरजी आये, वैसा
कर । तू जैसा करना चाहता है, वैसा कर - ऐसा कहने में
भी भगवान्‌की आत्मीयता, कृपालुता और हितैषिता ही
प्रत्यक्ष दीख रही है।
पहले ‘वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः' (७ । २), 'इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं
प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे' (९| १ ); 'वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया
(१० । १) आदि श्लोकोंमें भगवान् अर्जुनके हितकी बात
कहते आये हैं, पर इन वाक्योंमें भगवान्‌की अर्जुनपर
'सामान्य कृपा' है।
'न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ' ( १८ । ५८ ) - इस श्लोकमें
,
१ - योगयुक्त बुद्धिवाले कर्मफलका त्याग करके अनामय पदको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं (दूसरे अध्यायका इक्यावनवाँ श्लोक );
जो प्राप्ति ज्ञानयोगसे होती है, वह प्राप्ति कर्मयोगसे हो जाती है (चौथे अध्यायका अड़तीसवाँ श्लोक ); योगयुक्त मुनि बहुत
जल्दी परमात्माको प्राप्त हो जाता है ( पाँचवें अध्यायका छठा श्लोक ); कर्मफलका त्याग करनेपर सदा रहनेवाली शान्ति
प्राप्त होती है ( पाँचवें अध्यायका बारहवाँ श्लोक ) आदि श्लोकोंसे कर्मयोग परमात्मप्राप्तिका स्वतन्त्र साधन सिद्ध होता है ।
ऐसे कर्मयोगको 'गुह्य' कहते हैं ।
जडतासे सम्बन्ध-विच्छेद करके निराकार परमात्माके शरण हो जाना - यह कर्मयोगसे भी अधिक महत्त्वका है, इसलिये
इसे 'गुह्यतर' कहते हैं ।
सूर्यको मैंने ही उपदेश दिया था, वही मैं तेरेको कह रहा हूँ ( चौथे अध्यायका तीसरा श्लोक ); सम्पूर्ण जगत् मेरेसे ही
व्याप्त है (नवें अध्यायका चौथा श्लोक ); क्षरसे अतीत और अक्षरसे उत्तम 'पुरुषोत्तम' मैं ही हूँ ( पन्द्रहवें अध्यायका
अठारहवाँ श्लोक ) आदि बातोंमें भगवान्ने अपनी भगवत्ता प्रकट की है, इसलिये ये बातें 'गुह्यतम' हैं।
तू केवल मेरी ही शरणमें आ जा, फिर तेरेको किंचिन्मात्र भी करना नहीं है, मैं तेरेको सम्पूर्ण पापोंसे मुक्त कर दूँगा, तू शोक-
चिन्ता मत कर (अठारहवें अध्यायका छाछठवाँ श्लोक ) – इस प्रकार अपनी शरणागतिकी बात कहना 'सर्वगुह्यतम' है।
जिसमें कर्मयोग, ज्ञानयोग, भक्तियोग आदि सब साधनोंका वर्णन होता है, उस योगशास्त्रको 'परमगुह्य' कहा गया है
( अठारहवें अध्यायका अड़सठवाँ और पचहत्तरवाँ श्लोक ) ।
२ - गीतामें भक्तिकी बातें इन श्लोकोंमें आयी हैं- सम्पूर्ण योगियोंमें भक्तियोगी श्रेष्ठ है (छठे अध्यायका सैंतालीसवाँ
श्लोक ); मेरी शरण लेनेवाले मायाको तर जाते हैं ( सातवें अध्यायका चौदहवाँ श्लोक ); सब कुछ वासुदेव ही है - इस प्रकार
मेरी ( भगवान्‌की) शरण लेनेवाले महात्मा अत्यन्त दुर्लभ हैं ( सातवें अध्यायका उन्नीसवाँ श्लोक ); अनन्य भक्तिसे मैं सुलभ
हूँ (आठवें अध्यायका चौदहवाँ श्लोक ); अनन्यभक्तिसे परम पुरुषकी प्राप्ति होती है (आठवें अध्यायका बाईसवाँ श्लोक );
दैवी-सम्पत्तिके आश्रित महात्मालोग अनन्यमनसे मेरा भजन करते हैं (नवें अध्यायका तेरहवाँ श्लोक ); दृढ़ निश्चयवाले भक्त
निरन्तर कीर्तन करते हुए तथा मुझे नमस्कार करते हुए भक्तिपूर्वक मेरी उपासना करते हैं (नवें अध्यायका चौदहवाँ श्लोक );
अनन्यभक्तका योगक्षेम मैं वहन करता हूँ ( नवें अध्यायका बाईसवाँ श्लोक ); भक्तद्वारा प्रेमपूर्वक अर्पित पत्र, पुष्प, फल
आदिको मैं खाता हूँ (नवें अध्यायका छब्बीसवाँ श्लोक ); तू जो करता है, हवन करता है, दान देता है और तप करता है,
वह सब मेरे अर्पण कर ( नवें अध्यायका सत्ताईसवाँ श्लोक ); सब कर्म मेरे अर्पण कर दे तो तू शुभाशुभ फलरूप बन्धनसे

* The Saviour of the Saviours *
The Lord says to Arjuna, 'Tell me, Arjuna, that you have thoroughly thought over the things I have previously said about devotion.' The Lord has spoken about His devotion (sharanagati) in the seventieth to eighty-second verses of this chapter. One should take those words as 'etad' (this). Wherever devotion is spoken of in the Gita, one should take it as 'asheshen' (all). There is a deep mystery in the Lord's saying 'vimrshya etad asheshen' (considering all these things). The Lord is saying this so that Arjuna may not turn away from Him. If Arjuna considers these things carefully, he will certainly understand the truth, and he will not turn away from the Lord. 'Yathachchhasi tatha kuru' - After considering all these things carefully, do as you please. Do as you think fit. The Lord's saying this also shows His affection, His benevolence, and His interest in Arjuna. Earlier, in the seventh chapter, the Lord said, 'I will tell you all this in detail' (7.2). In the ninth chapter, He said, 'I will tell you this most secret thing, O ungrudging one' (9.1). In the tenth chapter, He said, 'I will tell you this, which is for your benefit' (10.1). In these verses, the Lord's words to Arjuna are general words of kindness. In the fifty-eighth verse of the eighteenth chapter, the Lord says, 'You will not hear (this) and you will not understand (this)' (18.58). In this verse, the Lord says that the yogi who has a purified intellect, who has renounced the fruits of his actions, attains the unblemished state (2.51). The attainment that is obtained through jnana-yoga is also obtained through karma-yoga (4.33). The yogi who has renounced the fruits of his actions attains peace that is eternal (5.12). Thus, karma-yoga is proved to be an independent means of attaining the Supreme. This karma-yoga is called 'guhya' (secret). The renunciation of the ego and the attainment of the unmanifest, formless Supreme is called 'guhyatara' (more secret). In the fourth chapter, the Lord says, 'I taught the sun (the sun god) this very thing, and I am teaching it to you' (4.3). In the ninth chapter, He says, 'The whole universe is pervaded by Me' (9.4). In the fifteenth chapter, He says, 'I am the supreme person, beyond the perishable and the imperishable' (15.18). In these verses, the Lord reveals His divinity. Therefore, these words are 'guhyatam' (most secret). You should take refuge in Me alone. I will free you from all sins. Do not worry or grieve (18.66). This is the essence of sharanagati (devotion). The yoga-shastra that contains the description of all the means of yoga, including karma-yoga, jnana-yoga, and bhakti-yoga, is called 'parama-guhyam' (most secret) (18.64 and 70). In the Gita, the following verses speak of devotion: 'Among all yogis, the devotee is the best' (6.46). 'Those who take refuge in Me cross over the ocean of Maya' (7.14). 'All this is Vasudeva' - those who take refuge in Me are very rare (7.19). 'I am easily attained by those who have unflinching devotion' (8.14). 'Through unflinching devotion, one attains the Supreme Person' (8.22). 'Those who are dependent on divine grace and who worship Me with unflinching devotion' (9.13). 'Those who worship Me with devotion, who constantly chant and offer obeisances to Me, and who offer Me their love and devotion' (9.14). 'I take care of the welfare of those who are devoted to Me' (9.22). 'I accept the offerings of those who are devoted to Me, including flowers, fruits, and other things' (9.26). 'You do whatever you do, offer it to Me' (9.27). 'If you offer all your actions to Me, you will be free from the bondage of good and bad karma' (9.28). 'You should offer your mind and intellect to Me alone, and you will attain Me' (9.34). 'Through unflinching devotion, one becomes beyond the three gunas' (14.26). 'The devotee who worships Me in all aspects is all-knowing' (15.19).

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

[ Chapter 18 ]

In the context of Arjuna's warning, the Lord's words 'yathācchāshti tathā kuru' (do as you please) and 'na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi' (you will neither hear nor perish) indicate the Lord's special grace and affection. However, Arjuna is still perturbed, thinking that the Lord is abandoning him. Arjuna thinks, "I have committed a grave mistake by not speaking up when the Lord was explaining things to me with love and affection, and even when He was telling me to take refuge in the Supreme Being. Now, I am not worthy of speaking up."

The Lord, without asking Arjuna, begins to speak the most confidential words:

Listen again, O Arjuna, to My most confidential and supreme words, for you are dear to Me and I will tell you what is beneficial for you. (64)

Translation of the shloka:

sarva-guhya-tamam = the most confidential and supreme
bhūyaḥ = again
śṛṇu = listen
me = to Me
paramam = the most confidential
vacah = words
iṣṭaḥ = dear friend
asī = you are
dṛḍham = firmly
iti = thus
tataḥ = therefore
vakṣyāmi = I will tell
te = to you
hitam = what is beneficial

Parishishta Bhaav (Appendix):

The Lord says, "I will tell you the most confidential and supreme words again, for you are dear to Me and I will tell you what is beneficial for you." The Lord had already mentioned the most confidential and supreme words in the 63rd shloka, but now He is saying that He will tell Arjuna something even more confidential and supreme. The Lord had previously said that the most confidential and supreme words are not to be spoken in public (tīrṣaṭasamā) and that they should not be spoken to those who are not devoted to Him (idam te na ātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācan). However, in the 56th shloka, the Lord had said, "sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja" (abandon all duties and take refuge in Me), which is the most confidential and supreme words. The Lord is saying that He will tell Arjuna something even more confidential and supreme than what He had previously said.

[Verse 63]

This is a very profound and secret teaching. *
Sadhak-Sanjivani *
In the second chapter, seventh verse, Arjuna calls himself 'dharma-sammoodha-cheta' (a person bewildered by dharma) and says that he is not capable of making a decision about dharma. He asks Lord Krishna for guidance, becomes his disciple, and requests him to teach him. Therefore, Lord Krishna says in this verse (sixty-fourth) that Arjuna should not take upon himself the burden of making decisions about dharma. He should leave that burden to Lord Krishna and dedicate himself to him alone. If Arjuna does so, Lord Krishna will free him from all sins and worries. This is the 'sarva-guhya-tam param vachan' (the most confidential and supreme teaching). The phrase 'bhuya shrunu' means that Lord Krishna has already said this in different words earlier, but Arjuna did not pay attention. Therefore, Lord Krishna is repeating the same thing again. Now, Arjuna should pay special attention to this. This teaching was first given by Lord Krishna in the following verses: 'mat-parah sarva-bhutanam janma-karma-phala-pradam' (18.57) and 'sarva-durgani mat-prasada-at tari-shyasi' (18.58). However, the phrase 'sarva-guhya-tam' was not used earlier, and Arjuna did not understand its significance. Therefore, Lord Krishna is using this phrase now to emphasize the importance of this teaching and to make Arjuna understand it. When Arjuna heard this, fear arose in his mind that Lord Krishna was abandoning him. To dispel this fear, Lord Krishna says that Arjuna is his most beloved friend. If Arjuna had no fear or doubt in his mind, there would have been no need for Lord Krishna to say, 'You are my most beloved friend.' Lord Krishna says this only when there is fear, doubt, or uncertainty in someone's mind. The phrase 'ishta' means that Lord Krishna considers his devotee as his own beloved deity. The devotee, in turn, considers Lord Krishna as his only deity and gives up everything else. Lord Krishna also considers his devotee as his own beloved deity, as it is said in the Gita: 'ye yatha maam prapadyante tams tathaiva bhajamy aham' (4.11). In the Bhagavatam, Lord Krishna says to Uddhava: 'You are as dear to me as my own self. There is no one else as dear to me as you. Not even Brahma, not even Shiva, not even Balarama, and not even Lakshmi, who resides in my body, is as dear to me as you are.' (11.14.15)

The phrase 'dridham' means that once Arjuna has said, 'I am your devotee' (in the second chapter, seventh verse), he should not have any fear or doubt. Lord Krishna has already said that he will protect his devotee from all dangers. Therefore, Lord Krishna says, 'You are my most beloved friend, and you should not have any fear.'

In the tenth chapter, Lord Krishna said, 'bhuya eva mahabaho shrinu me param vachan' (10.1). In this verse, Lord Krishna says, 'sarva-guhya-tam bhuya shrunu me param vachan' (18.63). The only difference is that in the tenth chapter, Lord Krishna said 'eva mahabaho' (again, O mighty-armed one), while in this verse, he says 'sarva-guhya-tam' (the most confidential and supreme). The rest of the words are the same. In the tenth chapter, Lord Krishna said, 'yad te 'ham prityamanaya vakshyami hita-kamyaya' (10.1). In this verse, Lord Krishna says, 'tato vakshyami te hitam' (18.63). In the ninth chapter, Lord Krishna said, 'man mana bhava' (9.34) without any pause. In this verse, Lord Krishna says, 'sarva-guhya-tam bhuya shrunu me param vachan' (18.63) without any pause. The phrase 'sarva-dharm-an parityajya mam ekam sharanam vraja' (18.66) is used only once in the Gita. 2. Saa sati kari puni karahe pasau. Naath prabhuinh kar sajju subhaau. 3. * Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]
'Then I shall tell you what is beneficial for you.' - You are my extremely dear one. Any object, person, event, situation, or state in the world is a friend, so I will tell you the most confidential and excellent thing in my heart. Another thing is that when I will tell you about taking refuge, it is not that I will benefit from it, but it will be beneficial for you. This proves that the benefit of a living being is only in taking refuge in God alone, without depending on anyone else. If a person is not steady, then how can their support be steady? Their support will not remain, but anxiety, sorrow, and pain will remain. Just as a spark is extinguished by water, it becomes a black coal - 'Coal does not become white, even if a hundred pounds of soap are applied.' But when that coal again meets fire, it becomes a spark (fire-like) and shines. Similarly, the living being becomes a spark (fire-like) and shines when it meets God. If the living being turns away from God, it is born and dies repeatedly and experiences pain. The living being finds no peace anywhere except in taking refuge in God. When the living being takes refuge in God, it becomes a little bit beneficial. The reason is that the living being is directly God's part, and it is not separate from God. Therefore, when the living being takes refuge in God, it becomes God-like and shines. If the living being takes refuge in anyone else, their support will not remain. When the living being takes refuge in God, it becomes a benefactor of the world. Parishishta Bhaav - 'Go to the shelter of the Unmanifest' (18.62) - This is the shelter of the Unmanifest, and 'Come to my shelter' (18.66) - This is the shelter of the Manifest. Taking refuge in the Unmanifest will lead to liberation, but taking refuge in the Manifest will lead to liberation along with love. Therefore, taking refuge in the Manifest is the 'most confidential'. God speaks 'param vachan' only in the context of devotion. In the first verse of the tenth chapter, God also said - 'Listen to my supreme word'. Arjuna had said to God that he is his disciple - 'I am your disciple' (2.7), but God says that he is his beloved - 'You are my beloved!' The meaning is that the guru makes the disciple, but God makes the disciple his friend. You are my beloved, and every word of God is beneficial, but there is a special beneficial thing in it, so God says 'Then I shall tell you what is beneficial for you.'

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

To be a devotee is to be a life-giving force. I am the Lord, and the Lord is mine; I am not of the world, and the world is not mine.' [When ego changes, attachment also changes of its own accord.]

One should change one's ego in the same way that a devotee does, because the Lord is the supreme well-wisher of all living beings, and whatever He does is for their welfare. Therefore, the Lord sends favorable or unfavorable circumstances, destroys the good and bad deeds of living beings, and makes them pure, and then attracts them to His lotus feet with great determination - this is the way to bow down to the Lord's lotus feet. 'Be my mind' - when one considers oneself to be the Lord's, the mind naturally becomes attached to the Lord. For what is one's own is naturally dear, and where there is affection, the mind naturally becomes attached. Therefore, when one considers oneself to be the Lord's, the Lord becomes naturally dear. Then, from the mind, one naturally thinks of the Lord's name, qualities, power, and pastimes. The Lord's name and form are meditated upon with great devotion and attachment. 'Madyaji' - when one changes one's ego, i.e., when one considers oneself to be the Lord's, all worldly activities become transformed into the Lord's service. That is, the devotee, who earlier used to do worldly work, now does the Lord's work. As the devotee's relationship with the Lord becomes stronger, his service attitude becomes transformed into a worshipful attitude. Then, whether he does worldly work, household work, or bodily work, or any other work, in all of it, he has the attitude of worshiping the Lord. His firm conviction is that there is no work other than the Lord's worship. 'Man namaskuru' - one should completely surrender to the Lord by bowing down to His lotus feet with eightfold prostration. I am fallen at the Lord's lotus feet - with this attitude, whatever favorable or unfavorable circumstances arise, one should consider the Lord's benevolent plan and remain pleased. Whatever the Lord does for me, it will be benevolent. Whether the circumstances are understood or not, this is a different matter, but the Lord's plan is always beneficial for me. Therefore, whatever happens, it is not the result of my actions, but the Lord's benevolent plan, sent for my benefit through His grace. 'Priyo'si me' - the Lord says, 'I promise you that by becoming my devotee, by considering yourself to be my own, by worshiping me, and by bowing down to me, you will attain me, i.e., you will reside in me.'

The meaning of 'priyo'si me' is that the Lord has immense affection for all living beings. No living being is unloved by the Lord, because they are all His own parts. The Lord sends them to 84 lakh different species or to hell, but His intention is always to purify them. This benevolent plan of the Lord is a sign of His love. To express this, the Lord makes Arjuna a representative of all living beings and says 'priyo'si me'. All living beings are very dear to the Lord. Only living beings consider the world (wealth, family, body, senses, mind, intellect, and life force, etc.) to be their own, whereas the world has never considered living beings to be its own. Living beings alone establish a relationship with the world. The world is constantly changing, while living beings are eternal and unchanging. The mistake of living beings is that they consider their relationship with the world to be eternal. This mistaken relationship remains even when the world is not present. This mistaken relationship is the cause of all troubles. One is free to accept or reject this relationship. Therefore, one should give up this mistaken relationship and take shelter in the Lord, who is our true and eternal friend. Parishishta Bhaav - Arjuna is already the Lord's, so the meaning of 'mamevaishyasi' is that one will attain the Lord's complete (mama) possession, which the Lord had mentioned at the beginning of the seventh chapter - 'Asamsayam samagram mam'. The Lord's devotion, attachment to Him, worship of Him, and bowing down to Him - if any one of these is done properly, the other three will automatically follow. (Translation ends here)

Take refuge in Me alone. Explanation - The Lord says, "Abandoning all duties and take refuge in Me alone." This means that one should give up the consideration of what to do and what not to do, and take shelter in Me alone. To take shelter in the Lord is the essence of all spiritual practices. In this state, the devotee has no more responsibilities; just as a devoted wife has no more responsibilities, she only thinks of her husband. She takes care of her body, her home, her family, her possessions, and her children, all for the sake of her husband. She considers her body, her home, her family, and her possessions as belonging to her husband, not to herself. In the same way, the devotee who takes shelter in the Lord considers his body, his family, his social status, and his name as belonging to the Lord, and he becomes fearless, free from anxiety, and without any doubts. According to the Gita, the word "dharma" here refers to duty or action. This is because in this chapter, from the 41st to the 42nd shloka, the word "svabhavaja karma" (natural action) has appeared, then in the first half of the 38th shloka, the word "svadharma" (one's own duty) has appeared, and finally, in the last shloka of the chapter and in the 44th shloka, the word "karma" (action) has appeared. Therefore, it is clear that the word "dharma" refers to duty or action. Now, the question arises whether the phrase "sarvadharmaan parityagy" means abandoning duty or action in its true form. The answer is that abandoning duty or action in its true form is neither in accordance with the Gita nor in accordance with the context of this chapter. Because, after hearing the Lord's words, Arjuna did not abandon his duty or action, but rather said, "I will do what you say" (18.73), and accepted the Lord's command to perform his duty or action. He not only accepted it, but also performed it according to his kshatriya dharma. Therefore, the phrase "sarvadharmaan parityagy" does not mean abandoning duty or action. The Lord Himself cannot say that one should abandon duty or action! In this very chapter, the Lord has said in the 6th shloka that one should never abandon the duties of yajna, dana, tapas, and one's own varna-ashrama, but rather one should always perform them. * In the third chapter, the Lord has said that one should never abandon duty or action - it is a must to perform duty or action; no one can remain without performing any action, not even for a moment (3.4); one who abandons action and thinks of worldly objects, he does not attain liberation or perfection (3.25);

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

It is clear from a thorough study of the Gita that a man should never abandon his duty or action in any circumstances. Arjuna considered it the best to abandon the duty of war and beg for alms (Second Chapter, Fifth Verse); but the Lord prohibited it (Second Chapter, Verses 31 to 38). This also proves that there is no abandonment of duty here. Now, we have to think what should be gained by abandoning all duties? According to the Gita, the best duty is to offer all actions to the Lord. In this, both the abandonment of the shelter of all duties and the taking of the shelter of the Lord are established. Those who take the shelter of duty are repeatedly born and die - 'and those who are engaged in the threefold duties attain to birth and death' (Gita 9.21). Therefore, by abandoning the shelter of duty and taking the shelter of the Lord alone, there is no need to decide about one's duty. This was also the case in Arjuna's life. |
I am free and engaged in another task. At such a time, it is proper for a charioteer not to shoot an arrow. You are a knower of weapons and the scriptures, and you know duty, so it is not proper to attack me.' After hearing Karan's words, Arjuna did not shoot the arrow. Then the Lord said to Karan, 'It is a duty to kill such a wicked person, not a sin * and just now you have killed Abhimanyu with six great charioteers, who had surrounded him alone. Therefore, there is no benefit in crying out for duty. Yes, it is a fortunate thing that at this time you are remembering the duty, but he who does not himself follow duty, has no right to cry out for duty.' Saying this, the Lord gave Arjuna permission to shoot the arrow, and Arjuna began to shoot the arrow. In this way, if Arjuna had decided about duty by his own intellect, he would have erred; therefore, he left the decision about duty to the Lord, and the Lord decided about duty. Arjuna had a doubt in his mind that for us, is it proper to fight or not to fight (Second Chapter, Sixth Verse). While Arjuna was fighting with Karan, the wheel of Karan's chariot got stuck in the ground. Karan got down from the chariot and said to Arjuna, 'Stay there, because you are on the chariot and I am on the ground.' (First Chapter, Forty-first to Forty-second Verses). He was a deceiver (Sixth Verse); he who controls his mind and senses and performs his duty is the best (Seventh Verse); one cannot maintain his body without performing actions, therefore, one should perform actions (Eighth Verse); one should not abandon actions due to fear of bondage, because the performance of duty alone is not binding, but to perform actions for one's own sake is binding (Ninth Verse); Brahma created the creation of the subjects along with duty and said that through this duty alone the subjects will increase and this duty will give them the means of livelihood (Tenth Verse); both men and gods will attain happiness by performing their duty (Eleventh Verse); one who performs duty without attachment is a thief (Twelfth Verse); one who performs duty and maintains his body is freed from all sins, and one who performs duty only for his own sake is a sinner who eats sin (Thirteenth Verse); the performance of duty alone keeps the cycle of creation going; but one who remains in the creation and does not perform his duty is a waste of life (Sixteenth Verse); one who performs duty without attachment attains the Supreme (Nineteenth Verse); even the wise Janaka and others have attained perfection by performing duty; from the point of view of the welfare of the people, one should also perform duty (Twentieth Verse); the Lord sets an example and says that if I do not perform duty with caution, I will become the cause of the downfall of the varna and the destruction of the people (Twenty-third to Twenty-fourth Verses); a wise man should perform duty like an ignorant man, without attachment (Twenty-fifth Verse); a wise man should perform duty in such a way that he does not create a distinction in the intellect of the ignorant (Twenty-sixth Verse). In this way, the Lord has emphasized the performance of duty in the third chapter. * One should kill an evil-doer even without thinking, for there is no fault in killing an evil-doer. * (Manu 8.350-351)

[ Chapter 18
We see on the other side that for a Kshatriya, the glory of war is described by God here, telling the entire essence of the Gita-

There is no greater means of achieving excellence. Therefore, God says, "What to do and what not to do, what is dharma and what is adharma, why are you getting entangled in this mess? Leave the burden of making decisions about dharma on me. This is the meaning of 'sarva-dharmān parityajya'."

'Mām ekam śaraṇaṃ vraja' - In these verses, the word 'ekam' cannot be a qualifying word for 'mām' (God); because 'mām' is one, not many. Therefore, the meaning of the word 'ekam' is 'ananya' (without a second). Another thing, Arjuna had also asked in 'tad ekam vada nishchitya' (3.2) and 'yacchreya etayor ekam' (5.1) about the means of achieving excellence in Sankhya and Karma Yoga, using the word 'ekam' (one). God wants to tell here that in all the means of achieving God, including Sankhya Yoga, Karma Yoga, etc., the main means is only one - ananya śaraṇa (unconditional surrender). In the Gita, Arjuna had asked many questions about the means of achieving his own well-being, and God had also given him answers. Looking at the Gita from the beginning to the end, it is clear that the essence of all means and the supreme means is to take refuge in God. |
'Mām ekam śaraṇaṃ vraja.' This means that I am the means and the goal. The meaning of 'Mām ekam śaraṇaṃ vraja' is not that one should take refuge in God through the intellect and the mind, but rather that one should surrender oneself to God. Because when one surrenders oneself to God, the mind, intellect, senses, body, etc. all become one with God, and do not remain separate. 'Ahṃ tvā sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ' - Some people may think that in this verse, God is offering Arjuna a promise to free him from the sins he had mentioned in the first chapter. But this interpretation is not logical; because when Arjuna had completely surrendered himself to God, how could he have any sins left, and how could God offer him a promise to free him from those sins? Therefore, this promise is not being offered after Arjuna has surrendered himself to God, but rather before he has surrendered. The meaning of 'I will free you from all sins' is that when you have completely surrendered yourself to me and have not yet seen any change in your thoughts, behavior, etc., do not worry or be afraid. Because when you have surrendered yourself to me, the lack of devotion, the lack of knowledge, the lack of purity, etc. are not your faults, but mine. Now it is my responsibility to remove those faults, to purify you. Your only responsibility is to remain fearless, free from worry, free from doubt, and to surrender yourself to my feet. But if you start to feel fear, worry, doubt, etc. in your heart, those will become obstacles to your surrender, and all the burden will fall on you. God has praised the glory of ananya bhakti (unconditional devotion) in the Gita at many places. For example, in the 14th verse of the 7th chapter, it is said that the means to cross over the difficult Maya is ananya bhakti. In the 14th verse of the 8th chapter, it is said that I am easily accessible to those who have ananya chetā (unconditional devotion). In the 22nd verse of the 8th chapter, it is said that the attainment of the Supreme Person is possible only through ananya bhakti. In the 22nd verse of the 9th chapter, it is said that I take care of the welfare of those who have ananya bhakti. In the 24th verse of the 11th chapter, it is said that ananya bhakti is the means to see, know, and attain God. In the 6th-7th verse of the 12th chapter, it is said that I quickly liberate those who have ananya bhakti. In the 26th verse of the 14th chapter, it is said that ananya bhakti is the means to become gunātīta (beyond the gunas). Therefore, ananya bhakti is the greatest of all means. 1 - In this verse, the word 'eva' is a qualifier for ananya (unconditional). 2 - In this verse, the word 'ananyachetā' is a qualifier for ananya (unconditional). 3 - When the jiva (soul) comes to me with a pure heart, then all his sins are destroyed. (Mānāsa 5.44.1)
4 - Some people's devotion is due to their own strength, some people's devotion is due to their own behavior. The princess Kunwarī, trusting in Vyāsa, lies down with her feet spread out.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

Just as Vibhishana, the devotee of Lord Rama, takes shelter in the Lord's feet, the Lord considers Vibhishana's faults to be His own faults. Once, Vibhishana crossed the ocean and reached a village called Viprghosh. There, an unknown brahmin was killed, and the brahmins of that village gathered and severely beat Vibhishana, but he did not die. Then, the brahmins tied him with chains and took him to a cave and locked him inside. When Lord Rama came to know that Vibhishana was imprisoned, He immediately reached Viprghosh village in the Pushpaka Vimana and found Vibhishana and went to him. The brahmins showed great respect to Lord Rama and said, "Maharaj, this person has committed brahminicide. We have beaten him severely, but he did not die." Lord Rama said, "O brahmins! I have given Vibhishana the age and kingdom of Kalpavriksha. How can he be killed? And what is the need to kill him? He is My devotee. I am ready to give up My life for My devotee. The responsibility of a servant's fault lies with the master, i.e., the master is responsible for punishing the servant. Therefore, in place of Vibhishana, you should punish Me."

Seeing the Lord's devotion to His devotees, all the brahmins were amazed and took shelter in the Lord's feet. The meaning is that "I am the Lord, and the Lord is Mine" - this equality, eligibility, authority, etc. is not present in anything. This is the essence of all means. Even a small child can control the entire house with the power of his own self, i.e., when he cries at night, the whole family gets up and tries to calm him down. Therefore, one should look at the Lord's devotion with the power of one's own self, not looking at one's own eligibility, etc. 'Ma Shucha' means-

(1) You are worried about me by taking shelter in me, this is a sin against me, your pride, and a stain on your devotion. Not trusting me completely and still worrying about me is a sin against me. Worrying about one's own faults is actually one's own pride, because one can only worry about faults if one has the strength to remove them. However, if one worries about faults without the intention of removing them, then worrying is not a fault. Just as a small child sees a dog coming and cries, but does not worry, similarly, worrying about faults is not a fault, but worrying is a fault. Worrying means that one has the strength to rely on one's own self, and this is your pride. You are worried about me, your Lord, while taking shelter in me, so where will your worry go? People will see this and say, "This is the Lord's devotee, and he is worried!" The Lord will not remove your worry. You are worried about me without trusting me, so there is a lack of trust in you, and a stain on your devotion. Leave this aside. (2) Even if your thoughts, behavior, and actions are not pure, do not worry about them. I will take care of them. (3) In the seventh shloka of the second chapter, Arjuna takes shelter in the Lord, and in the eighth shloka, he says that even if he gets a kingdom full of wealth and grain, or becomes the king of the gods, his sorrow will not be removed. The Lord seems to be saying that your words are correct; because sorrow never goes away due to worldly, ephemeral things, nor can it, nor is it possible. However, taking shelter in me and still worrying about your sorrow is a great mistake. You are taking the burden of your sorrow on your own head. 1 - What is my death, if my devotee is killed? How can my devotee be killed? I have given him the kingdom and age of Kalpavriksha, and it will be the same in the future. In every case, the master is responsible for punishing the servant. The brahmins, hearing Lord Rama's words, were amazed and said this. (From Padma Purana, Patala 104, 150-151)

2 - When Draupadi's sari was torn in the assembly of the Kauravas, Draupadi held her sari with her hands and teeth and called out to the Lord. Relying on one's own strength, one calls out to the Lord, and it takes time for the Lord to come. However, when Draupadi completely gives up her efforts and relies only on the Lord, Dushasana tires of pulling her sari and the pile of sari threads accumulates, but none of Draupadi's limbs are exposed.

Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
(4) After taking refuge, a devotee should not worry about worldly or heavenly matters, or about good or bad fortune. A devotee has said, 'Let me be in heaven or on earth, or in hell, as You please. I am content with whatever You decide. Even in death, I will think of Your lotus feet, which are like the tender shoots of the Sharada tree. I will not forget Your feet.'

'Oh, Lord of the destroyers of hell! You may keep me in heaven, on earth, or in hell, as You please. Do whatever You want. I have no other request. My only prayer is that even in the most terrifying state of death, I will think of Your beautiful feet, which are beyond the beauty of the tender shoots of the Sharada tree. I will not forget Your feet.'

The special aspect of taking refuge
When a devotee takes refuge, he firmly believes, 'I am a servant of God, and God is my Master.' He accepts this feeling with conviction, and as a result, the roots of his fears, sorrows, worries, doubts, and other vices are cut off. This is because, from the devotee's point of view, all vices are rooted in the feeling of separation from God. Even when in the presence of God, the devotee's attachment to the world and the body remains, but when the devotee's attachment to God becomes firm, these attachments are completely eliminated. This is because the devotee's attachment to God is the root of all virtues. What is the firm attachment to God? It is the absence of fear, sorrow, worry, doubt, examination, and opposite feelings. Now, let us consider these one by one. (1) Fearlessness - Due to the lack of good conduct, fear arises from within, and fear arises from outside due to snakes, scorpions, tigers, etc. The two types of fear that a devotee experiences are completely eliminated. Even the fear of death, which Patanjali Maharaaj has considered the fifth klesha and which even great scholars experience, is completely eliminated. The fear that my virtues will be ruined - This fear should also be eliminated from within. Why? Because 'I have been purified by the mercy of God, and now I have no fear of anything. I could not purify these virtues by accepting them as mine; because accepting them as mine is the very cause of their impurity - 'Mamatamal jarai jai' (Mans 7.117). Therefore, I will never accept them as mine again. When these virtues are not mine, why should I fear anything? Now, it is only the mercy of God that is sufficient. The mercy of God is all-pervading.'

Many people have doubts that taking refuge in God and serving Him will lead to duality, i.e., God and the devotee will become two separate entities, and this will lead to fear. However, this doubt is baseless. Fear arises from the other, not from the self. The world and the body are the other, and as long as the devotee is attached to them, fear arises. But when the devotee's attachment to God becomes firm, the fear of the other is eliminated. (1) - When the world and the body's attachment is completely eliminated, the desire to live, the desire to act, and the desire to enjoy - these four desires do not remain. - 'The five afflictions are ignorance, egoism, attachment, aversion, and clinging to the notion of "I am" and "this is mine".' (Yogdarshan 2.3)
- 'Even the wise, who have attained the highest state, are attached to the notion of "I am".' (Yogdarshan 2.9)
- 'And the fear of death, Oh, Lord! Your devotees, who have a strong attachment to Your feet, never fall from the path. They roam fearlessly, protected by You, like the army of Lord Vinaayak, with their heads held high.' (Shrimad Bhagavat 10.2.33) 'Oh, Lord! They roam fearlessly, protected by You, like the army of Lord Vinaayak, with their heads held high.'

The Lord is not a second entity; He is the very own. One should never harbor such a feeling. If, due to some reason, such thoughts arise suddenly, then one should call out to the Lord with a sense of distress: "O my Lord! O my Master! Save me! Save me!! Save me!!!". Because He is my Master, my all-powerful Lord, why should I worry? And the Lord Himself has said, "Do not worry" (My dear pure one). Therefore, one should surrender to the Lord with a calm mind and say, "O Lord! This is all in Your hands; You know everything."

The jiva is an eternal part of the Lord, His very form. Therefore, how can there be fear of the Lord when one surrenders to Him? On the contrary, one becomes fearless forever. From a gross perspective, a child may feel fear when separated from its mother, but when it is in its mother's lap, the fear disappears because the mother is its own. A devotee of the Lord is unlike this. The reason is that there is a distinction between a child and its mother, but there is no distinction between a devotee and the Lord. (2) Not to grieve - Grief arises when one broods over what has already passed. To grieve over what has already passed is a grave mistake; because what has happened was inevitable, and what is not going to happen will never happen, and what is happening now is happening exactly as it should. Therefore, there is no reason to grieve. Knowing the Lord's benevolent will, a devotee who has surrendered to Him remains forever griefless; grief never comes to him. (3) To be free from anxiety - When a devotee surrenders himself, along with all his possessions, to the Lord, he is not anxious about anything, not even the slightest thing, whether it be worldly or otherworldly. He does not worry about how he will live, where he will live, what will be his fate, and so on. When one surrenders to the Lord, the devotee has one thought: "If my life is not worthy of the Lord, if it is not pure and beautiful, then how can the Lord's words be reflected in my behavior?" In reality, to think that one's nature is the cause of the problem is itself a mistake. It is not the nature that is the problem, but the fact that one identifies with the mind, intellect, senses, and body - this is the mistake. When one surrenders to the Lord, why should one worry about the impurities of the mind, intellect, and so on? It is a contradiction to worry about these things after surrendering to the Lord. Therefore, a devotee should think, "The Lord says, 'I will deliver you from all sins,' so why should I do anything to escape from these vices?" I am Yours, O Lord! I have never thought that these vices are mine. O Lord! I have never seen these body, senses, life, mind, and intellect as mine. But even after surrendering everything to You, O Lord, these body and so on sometimes appear to be mine. Now, O Lord, please deliver me from this sin - and thus one becomes free from anxiety. (4) To be free from doubt - One should never doubt whether one is the Lord's or not, whether the Lord has accepted one or not. Rather, one should think, "I have been the Lord's from time immemorial, I am the Lord's, and I will always be the Lord's." I have mistakenly thought that I am separate from the Lord. But even if I think that I am separate from the Lord, I can never be separate from Him, and it is not possible to be separate from Him. If I even want to be separate from the Lord, how can I be? Because the Lord has said, "This jiva is My own part" (Gita 15.7). Therefore, remembering the truth that "I am the Lord's and the Lord is mine," all doubts and fears disappear, and there is no room for doubts and fears. 1 - (1) Rama does what He wills, and that is what happens. If one does anything else, it is of no use. (Mansaghar 1.128.1)
(2) What Rama creates and preserves is what happens. One can try to argue and reason, but it is of no use. (Mansaghar 1.52.4)

2 - O merciful Lord, my mind is always filled with joy. I am Your servant, Rama, and I am always under Your protection.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18
(5) Not to be tested - After taking refuge in the Lord, one should not test oneself to see if one has such and such qualities. Instead, one should think, "If I have taken refuge in the Lord, then such and such qualities should be present in me." If such qualities are not present, then one should think, "I have not taken refuge in the Lord." On the other hand, if one sees that one lacks such qualities as "non-enmity" (advesha) etc. (as mentioned in the Gita, 12th chapter, 13th to 19th verses), one should be surprised and think, "How is it that I lack these qualities?" As soon as one thinks in this way, one's lack of these qualities will disappear. This is because one has the direct experience that one lacked these qualities to a greater extent before taking refuge in the Lord. After taking refuge, one's qualities, such as those of a devotee, will manifest automatically without any effort. (6) Not to have a contrary notion - It is not possible for a devotee who has taken refuge in the Lord to have a contrary notion, such as "I am not the Lord's." This notion is not dependent on one's acceptance or rejection of it. The relationship between the Lord and the individual is eternal, unbroken, and constant. One has not considered this relationship, and this was one's mistake. Now that this mistake has been rectified, how can one have a contrary notion? One who sincerely accepts the Lord's devotee as such will not have fear, sorrow, anxiety, etc. in their heart. Their devotion to the Lord will become firm of its own accord, just like the bond between a son and his father becomes firm of its own accord. The bond between a son and his father becomes firm to the extent that even in a dream, the son does not think, "I am not from this family." Their heart becomes firm in the thought, "I am a part of this family, and these are all mine." When the granddaughter of the son comes and creates chaos in the house, the grandmother says, "This outsider has ruined our house!" But the old grandmother does not even remember that she too is an outsider who was born in someone else's house. The point is that even in a superficial relationship, such as that between a son and his father, there can be such firmness. How much more so in the eternal and unbreakable relationship between the Lord and the individual! Therefore, it is not surprising that the devotee's relationship with the Lord becomes firm. In reality, the firmness of the relationship with the Lord can be achieved only by giving up the worldly relationships that are considered important in the world. If there is any deficiency in the devotee's qualities, behavior, etc., or if they develop a contrary attitude or commit some wrong action under duress, they will feel a sense of guilt in their heart. To illustrate this, a village story is told. A mother had three sons, two of whom were grown up and worked, while the third was simple-minded and innocent. The mother died, and the two elder brothers told the youngest, "Mother's ashes (sthulas) should be immersed in the Ganges." The youngest son said, "That's fine." He took the ashes and set out on the 300-kos journey to the Ganges. As he walked, he got tired and asked someone, "Brother, how far is the Ganges?" The person replied, "You have already covered 150 kos, and there are 150 kos more to go." The youngest son thought, "How will I reach the Ganges and then return?" Feeling sad, he threw the ashes into the jungle and brought back a pot of sweet water from the nearby village well, thinking that the Ganges water would be available on the way back. He returned to the village and told his brothers, "I have immersed the ashes in the Ganges and brought back the Ganges water." The elder brothers thought, "If he had really gone to the Ganges, he would not have returned so soon." They asked him, "Did you really go to the Ganges?" He replied, "Yes, I went and immersed the ashes in the Ganges." The elder brothers realized that he was not telling the truth and remained silent. The next day, one of the elder brothers woke up and asked the youngest, "Tell me the truth, did you really go to the Ganges and immerse the ashes?" The youngest replied, "Yes, I went and immersed the ashes in the Ganges." The elder brother said, "I had a dream last night, and in the dream, my mother said that you did not take the ashes to the Ganges, but threw them away on the way." The youngest brother asked, "Why did mother come to me and not to you?" The elder brother replied, "You had already covered 150 kos, so why did she not go 150 kos further and reach the Ganges?" The youngest brother said, "If she had gone 150 kos further, she would not have come back to me, but would have gone to the Ganges." The point of this story is that after taking refuge in the Lord, one is tested to see if one has the qualities of a devotee. If one does not have these qualities, one should think, "I have not taken refuge in the Lord." This is the opposite of the notion that "I have taken refuge in the Lord, so I should have these qualities." If one has this notion, one will be deceived."
