* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

The devotee who has surrendered to the Lord will never have to do anything for himself; because he has completely surrendered his own self, along with all his possessions, to the Lord, who is the true owner of everything. Now, all actions, whether easy or difficult, and all circumstances, will be taken care of by the Lord. 2
The Lord looks upon His devotees as His own, and not at their virtues or vices. This is because the devotee is eternally the Lord's own, and the vices are only temporary. Therefore, the Lord's vision is always focused on the reality of the devotee's eternal relationship with Him. Just as a mother's vision is focused on her child, and not on the dirt that covers it, so the Lord's vision is focused on His devotee, and not on their vices. Just as Draupadi was filled with hatred and anger when she thought of washing her hair with the blood of Dushasan, but when she called out to the Lord, He appeared immediately, because she had a deep and abiding relationship with Him. The devotee who has surrendered to the Lord has no need to do anything for himself; because he has given up everything, including his own ego, to the Lord, who is the true owner of everything. Just as Kakabhushundi, the devotee, was filled with joy and satisfaction when he was told by the Lord that he would be a devotee of Rama, and that he would be blessed with all good qualities, and that he would be able to attain whatever he desired, so the devotee who has surrendered to the Lord will always be filled with joy and satisfaction, regardless of the circumstances. The Lord's devotee has two feelings: (1) the Lord is mine, and (2) I am the Lord's. In both cases, the devotee's relationship with the Lord is the same, but in the first case, the devotee may have a desire to please the Lord, and in the second case, the devotee has no desire to please the Lord, because he knows that the Lord will do what is best for him. Therefore, the devotee should give up his own desires and will, and surrender completely to the Lord. The devotee who has surrendered to the Lord will never have to worry about his own salvation; because the Lord will take care of everything. Just as the Lord took care of Kakabhushundi, the devotee, and blessed him with all good qualities, and told him that he would be a devotee of Rama, and that he would be able to attain whatever he desired, so the devotee who has surrendered to the Lord will always be blessed with all good qualities, and will be able to attain whatever he desires. 1
The Lord is the supreme refuge of the devotee who has surrendered to Him, and He is the destroyer of all sins. If the devotee commits any sin, the Lord will destroy it completely. (Shrimad Bhagavatam 11.5.42)

The devotee who has surrendered to the Lord will always be filled with joy and satisfaction, and will never be worried about his own salvation. He will always be in a state of ecstasy, and will always be filled with love for the Lord. (Mansaghar 7.114)

2
The Lord is always present in the heart of the devotee who has surrendered to Him, and He is always watching over him. The devotee will never be separated from the Lord, and will always be filled with joy and satisfaction. (Mansaghar 1.29.3)

Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18
Here, the phrase 'bhajan pratap' means - what remains to be done according to the will of God. There is a flutter in the heart of God for the welfare of living beings, that is why God says, 'sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja' (abandon all duties and take refuge in me), which is a very confidential thing. Because God considers living beings as friends - 'suhṛdaṃ sarva-bhūtānām' (5.29), and gives them the freedom to attain me through any of the means such as karma yoga, jnana yoga, bhakti yoga, etc. and to destroy suffering, sorrow, etc. for all time. A devotee remains happy at all times. Even in adverse circumstances, the happiness of a lover devotee increases more and more, because the nature of love is ever-increasing. It is a rule that what belongs to oneself is always dear to oneself. God considers all living beings as dear - 'sab mam priya sab mam upajaye' (Manas 7.86.2), and this living being is also dear to God. However, this living being forgets its dear Lord due to ignorance of the transitory world and the body. Even in this forgetfulness, God has not abandoned this living being and will never abandon it. Because this living being is eternally a part of God. Therefore, God's affection, compassion, love, benevolence, and impartial generosity towards all living beings are natural and unbroken. For this reason, God incarnates at various times to protect devotees, destroy the wicked, and establish dharma (5.24). In these three activities, there is only God's natural affection, otherwise, what purpose would God's protection of devotees, destruction of the wicked, and establishment of dharma serve? God performs these three activities only for the welfare of living beings. This also proves God's natural affection, compassion, love, benevolence, and impartial generosity towards living beings, and God says to Arjuna - 'mad-bhakto bhava, man-mana bhava, mad-yaji bhava, mam namaskuru' (become my devotee, think of me, worship me, and bow down to me). In these four things, God's intention is only to bring the living being before him, so that all living beings may turn away from transient objects. Because suffering, sorrow, repeated birth and death, and calamity are the main causes of living beings turning away from God. In reality, the liberation of the living being is only possible through God's grace. All means such as karma yoga, jnana yoga, bhakti yoga, etc. are revealed by God and great souls who know God's nature. Therefore, God's grace is the essence of all these means. The seeker is only a means, but God's grace is the main cause of the success of the means. A devotee who has taken shelter of God should never worry about things like - God has not yet shown himself, God's love has not yet been felt, the mind has not yet been purified, etc. This kind of worry is like a monkey's child. A monkey's child is always clinging to the monkey. The monkey jumps and leaps wherever it goes, but the child is always clinging to it. A devotee should leave all his worries with God, i.e., whether God shows himself or not, whether love is felt or not, whether the mind is purified or not, etc. He should be like a cat's child. A cat's child always depends on its mother. The cat can put it anywhere, take it anywhere, but the child always keeps its paws and legs folded, looking at its mother. Whatever a devotee does, he should do it considering it as God's work, considering God's power, and doing it for God's sake, not for his own sake - this is what it means to fold one's hands and legs.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

As a potter first lifts the clay on his head and brings it near; but this example is not complete; because the clay remains by the potter's side naturally; he does not make any effort to save it. But the devotees of the Lord, turning their backs on the world, take refuge in the Lord's feet. The implication is that one who considers himself a part of the Lord, yet considers the world as his own or desires something from it, is trapped in the cycle of birth and death and suffers. The potter's will is the same whether he moistens the clay and pounds it, or puts it on the wheel and spins it. The clay never says, "Make a pot, make a bowl, make a potter's wheel." The potter does as he pleases. Similarly, a devotee who has taken refuge in the Lord does not have his own will or desires. The more he is free from anxiety and fear, the more the Lord's grace takes hold of him, and the more he is anxious, the more he hinders the Lord's grace. Just as a fisherman casts a net in the river to catch fish, and all the fish caught in the net are trapped; but the fish that comes near the fisherman's feet is not caught. Similarly, the world is a net of the Lord's Maya, and those who are entangled in it are trapped in the cycle of birth and death; but those who take refuge in the Lord's feet are freed from Maya. "Those who take refuge in Me alone, they cross over this Maya" (Gita 7.14). One should only grasp this example; because the fisherman's intention is to catch fish in the net, but the Lord's intention is not to trap the jiva in Maya. The Lord's intention is to free the jiva from the net of Maya and take refuge in Him, and that is why He says, "Take refuge in Me alone."

The relationship between the world and the Lord is of two kinds. The world's relationship is only a concept, and the Lord's relationship is real. The world's relationship makes a person a slave, a servant, but the Lord's relationship makes a person free, divine, and the Lord's own property. If a person considers himself special because of his knowledge, wisdom, wealth, renunciation, or detachment, it is a sign of slavery, servitude. If a person considers himself special because of his wealth, it is a sign of slavery to wealth. The world's rule is that those who consider themselves special because of something, are reduced to nothing, are made lowly. But those who are dependent on the Lord, who always rely on the Lord, do not consider themselves special; instead, they see the Lord's uniqueness, His extraordinary nature, His wonder. The Lord can make a person His crown jewel or His property, but that person will not see himself as special. The Lord's rule is like a wheel, where all the grains that come near the center remain intact, but those that are far from the center are crushed. Similarly, the world's cycle is like a wheel, where all the jivas, the body, the senses, the mind, are crushed, are destroyed; but those who are dependent on the Lord, who are near the center, are not crushed; they are divine, and they are free from the cycle of birth and death. Just as the grains that are near the center of the wheel remain intact, so do the jivas who are dependent on the Lord. Some of them remain like this even in the end. Just as the body of a devotee who has merged with the Lord remains intact, as in the case of Mirabai, who merged with the Lord's form with her body, so does the body of a devotee who has merged with the Lord remain intact. As Kabir said, "Just as a grain of wheat remains intact in the mill, so does a devotee remain intact in the Lord."

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]
A small child, the son of the Lord, remained in the Lord's mouth, and nothing was left. Similarly, the saint Shri Tukaramji went to Vaikuntha with his body. They became one with the Lord. Only a piece of their sari was left, which was hanging on the branches and twigs of a tree. A creeper was spread over the tree's branches and twigs. The tender fibers of the creeper were spreading. New buds were sprouting on some of these fibers, and copper-colored leaves were emerging on others. The creeper was covered with flowers and leaves. The tree's beauty was enhanced by the creeper. The tree looked very pleasant. Seeing the tree's beauty, Lord Shri Ram said to Hanumanji, "Look, Hanuman! This creeper is so beautiful! It is covered with its beautiful fruits, fragrant flowers, and green leaves. It has enhanced the tree's beauty so much that it looks more beautiful than all the other trees in the forest. Moreover, it is because of this creeper that the entire forest is beautiful. It is because of this creeper that animals and birds take shelter under this tree. This creeper is blessed!"

In the path of knowledge, the body is not filled with consciousness; because the knower separates himself from the non-existent and becomes one with the conscious essence. However, when a devotee stands before the Lord, his body, senses, mind, and life force all stand before the Lord. The implication is that those whose vision is only on the conscious essence, i.e., those who do not see any independent existence, their consciousness pervades their body, and they become conscious. However, in the eyes of people, their body appears to be material, but in reality, it is conscious. When one takes shelter of the Lord, the Lord's mercy is especially evident towards the devotee. However, the mercy of Mother Lakshmi, who is the embodiment of love and is inseparable from the Lord, is even more. It is impossible to describe the love of Mother Lakshmi for the devotee. In worldly dealings, it is also seen that a devoted wife is very fond of her husband and children. Another thing is that when the Lord, filled with love, comes to see His devotee on the back of a garuda, Mother Lakshmi also sits with the Lord on the garuda, whose wings sing the Mantras of the Sama Veda. However, if someone does not want the Lord but only wants Mother Lakshmi, then Mother Lakshmi comes, but her vehicle is a blind owl. If a person considers Mother Lakshmi as an object of enjoyment, then he suffers a great downfall; because he only sees his mother with a distorted vision, and he becomes a great sinner. Hearing the praise of the creeper from Lord Shri Ram's mouth, Sita said to Hanuman, "Look, son Hanuman! Did you think of this? See, the creeper has climbed up, covered with flowers and leaves, and its fibers have spread. All these are dependent on the tree. The creeper's beauty is also due to the tree. Therefore, the tree's glory is the main thing. The tree is the foundation. Without the tree's support, the creeper cannot even climb up, nor can it cover itself with flowers and leaves. Now tell me, Hanuman! Is the glory not of the tree?"

Hanuman said, "We think of a third thing, mother."

Sita asked, "What is that, son?"

Hanuman said, "Mother, the shade of the tree and the creeper is very beautiful. Therefore, we like to live in the shade of you both, i.e., in the shelter of your feet."

Servant son, husband, mother, trust. Remain without worry, and be nourished by the Lord. (Mansa 4.3.2)

A third thing is that where there is only the Lord's love, the Lord and His divine, bliss-giving power, i.e., Mother Lakshmi, both become one and enhance each other's beauty. However, someone considers only Mother Lakshmi to be superior, and someone considers only the Lord to be superior. This is not a rule. There is a story about a devotee in this context. Ram and Hanuman were sitting under a tree in the forest.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

Once, a sage with a vision of knowledge (a blind man) was walking with a stick, whose footprints were visible. A lion came and saw them walking along the banks of the Yamuna River. The lion asked the river, "You are alone in the forest, how did you get here?" The river was swollen. The lion said, "Look at this footprint, then talk." The stick fell into the water, and the sage also fell into the water. The lion said, "I am the one whose footprint this is. I have taken refuge in you." The lion let go of the stick and gave the river an assurance, "Don't be afraid, be fearless." It seemed as if someone had picked them up and put them on the bank. Then another stick came into their hand, and they started walking. The meaning is that one who takes refuge in the Lord and remains dependent on Him, does not have to do anything for himself. Whatever the Lord does, he is pleased with that. Many sheep and goats went to the forest to graze. Among them, a goat got stuck in a tree. It took a long time for the goat to get out of the tree, and by then all the other sheep and goats had reached their homes. It was getting dark. The goat wandered and reached the bank of a lake. There was a footprint of a lion on the wet soil. The goat took refuge in that footprint and sat down. In the night, wild animals like jackals, wolves, tigers, and bears came to eat the goat, but the goat said, "First, see whose footprint this is, then eat me." They saw the footprint and said, "This is the footprint of a lion, run away quickly."

When a wild elephant came to the lake to drink water at night, the lion said to the elephant, "You take this goat on your back and take it to the forest and graze it, and always keep it on your back, otherwise, I will kill you!" The elephant was frightened and quickly picked up the goat on its back. The goat sat on the elephant's back and started eating the leaves of the trees and was very happy. It seemed as if someone had put it on the elephant's back. The meaning is that one who takes refuge in the Lord and holds onto His feet, becomes fearless and free from all obstacles. No one can frighten or harm him. Just as the elephant was frightened by the lion, so too, all living beings are frightened by the lion of fear. But one who takes refuge in the Lord, is not afraid of anyone. He is not harmed by anyone. Just as the elephant was forced to take the goat on its back, so too, one who takes refuge in the Lord, does not have to do anything for himself. The Lord takes care of him. Just as the elephant was forced to graze the goat, so too, one who takes refuge in the Lord, is always under His protection. The Lord says, "O sinless Uddhava! This is not just the case in one era, but in all eras, it is the same. Through my association, even demons, ghosts, animals, birds, Gandharvas, Apsaras, snakes, Siddhas, Charanas, Guhyakas, and Vidyadharas have attained me. (1) Many people have attained me through their attachment to me, fear of me, hatred towards me, and love for me, just like devotees through devotion. Just as Gopis attained me through their attachment, Kansa through fear, Shishupala and Dantavakra through hatred, Yadavas through family ties, and you people through love, and we through devotion."

(2) Through my association, even demons, ghosts, animals, birds, Gandharvas, Apsaras, snakes, Siddhas, Charanas, Guhyakas, and Vidyadharas have attained me. In every era, even the lowest of the low, women, and outcasts have attained me. Even those who are in the mode of ignorance and those who are in the mode of passion have attained me. Many people have attained me through their attachment to me, fear of me, hatred towards me, and love for me, just like devotees through devotion.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]
Those who have a connection with God in any way, without understanding, quickly interpret His words in a way that is opposite to their true meaning. Therefore, people who are worthy of hearing and speaking such words are very few. The Lord has mentioned two things about those who have taken refuge in Him in the Gita. Their salvation is already achieved, but those who have not connected with God in any way, remaining indifferent, have been deprived of attaining God. The Lord's exclusive devotees have been told by Nārada that there is no difference in them due to caste, education, beauty, family, wealth, and other such things. (Nārad Bhakti Sūtra 72)
"There is no difference in them due to caste, education, beauty, family, wealth, and other such things."

The meaning is that, taking the body as the basis, all the differences in the world, such as caste, education, and other such things, do not apply to those who are completely devoted to God. The reason is that they are the property of the infallible God, 'yatas tadīyāḥ' (Nārad Bhakti Sūtra 73), not of the world. Therefore, they are known as 'Achyut Gotra' (the family of the infallible God). The Secret of Taking Refuge
It has been said that:

(1) "Mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja" (18.66) "Come to me alone with an unshakeable devotion."
(2) "Sa sarva-vidha bhajati māṃ sarva-bhāvena bhārata" (15.19) "That omniscient person worships me with all his being," "Tam eva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarva-bhāvena bhārata" (18.62) "You go to that supreme being with all your being."

How can we take refuge in God? We should take refuge in God alone, without looking at His attributes, such as His beauty and power, and without having any worldly desires. The secret of taking refuge in God alone is that God has infinite attributes, powers, and secrets, and infinite beauty, majesty, and charm. The devotee who takes refuge in God does not look at these attributes; his only thought is that he is only a part of God and that he is only a devotee of God. The secret of taking refuge in God is known only to God Himself. However, an attempt is made to explain it in human language, as everyone who speaks tries to convey his own understanding. The readers are requested not to interpret the words in a way that is opposite to their true meaning, as people often do with philosophical and mysterious concepts. It is said that even those who are born in a low caste, are uneducated, or are of a low social status, can attain God through the power of devotion. The Lord Himself has said that His devotees are not bound by their birth, education, or social status. (Adhyatma 10.20)
"There is no difference in the devotees due to their birth, education, or social status. The only reason for their devotion is their love for God."

It is also said that even those who are not born in a high caste, are not educated, or do not have a good social status, can attain God through devotion. (Bhagavata 17)
"What is the use of being born in a high caste, or being educated, or having a good social status? The only thing that matters is that one's heart is always filled with devotion to God. There is no one else in this world who is as fortunate as one who has such devotion."

It is also said that even those who are born with a disability, are old, are uneducated, or are of a low social status, can attain God through devotion. (Padyaavali 8)
"What was the good quality of the diseased person? What was the great age of Dhruva? What was the knowledge of the elephant-headed person? What was the high caste of Vidura? What was the bravery of Yadupati Ugrasen? What was the beautiful form of the hunchbacked woman? What was the wealth of Sudama? Still, all these people attained God. The reason is that God is pleased only with devotion, not with good qualities, knowledge, or wealth."

Just as a girl is a part of her father's family, a devotee is a part of God's family through devotion. (Nārada Pancha Ratra)
".

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

If one takes refuge in the beginning itself, but not in the Lord, then one should not interpret these things in a reverse manner. If one takes refuge in the Lord, then in reality, the Lord's glory, influence, and other attributes will not be lost - this is not the case. They will remain the same. Similarly, if one takes refuge in the Lord solely due to His attributes, then the Lord's attributes, influence, and other attributes will be lost - this is not the case. However, our vision should only be on the Lord, not on His attributes. What is interpreting things in a reverse manner? Not accepting the Lord's attributes, influence, name, glory, wealth, sweetness, beauty, and other attributes, and not going towards them. Now, there is nothing to be done, nor is there any need to worship the Lord, nor is there any need to listen to the Lord's attributes, influence, and other attributes, nor is there any need to go to the Lord's abode - this is interpreting things in a reverse manner. This is a great mistake. The sole meaning of taking refuge in the Lord is that the Lord is mine alone. Now, if the Lord is wealthy and prosperous, it is a great good fortune, and if He is not wealthy and prosperous, it is also a great good fortune. If the Lord is very merciful, it is a great good fortune, and if He is very harsh and cruel, it is also a great good fortune. If the Lord has a great influence, it is a great good fortune, and if He has no influence, it is also a great good fortune. The one who takes refuge in the Lord does not worry about these things. His sole attitude is that the Lord, as He is, is mine. If one takes refuge in the Lord due to His attributes, influence, and other attributes, then the Lord's attributes, influence, and other attributes will be lost - this is not the case. However, if we do not worry about the Lord's attributes, influence, and other attributes, then our true refuge will be established. Where one takes refuge in the Lord due to His attributes, influence, and other attributes, there one does not take refuge in the Lord, but rather in His attributes, influence, and other attributes. Just as if someone respects a person due to their wealth, then in reality, it is not the person who is being respected, but their wealth. If someone respects a minister due to their position, then in reality, it is not the minister who is being respected, but their position. If someone respects a strong person due to their strength, then in reality, it is not the person who is being respected, but their strength. However, if someone respects a person solely due to their wealth, then this does not bring any benefit to the wealthy person. Similarly, if someone respects a minister solely due to their position, then this does not bring any benefit to the minister. If someone respects a strong person solely due to their strength, then this does not bring any benefit to the strong person. However, if someone takes refuge in the Lord solely due to His attributes, influence, and other attributes, then this does not bring any benefit to the Lord. On the other hand, if someone takes refuge in the Lord solely due to His love, then this brings great benefit to the Lord. The Lord sees that the person is devoted to Him, not to His attributes, influence, and other attributes, and therefore, the Lord has great respect for that person. (1) "My beloved Lord Shri Krishna, even if He is ugly or beautiful, even if He is devoid of qualities or is the best among the qualified, even if He is envious of me or is the ocean of mercy, He is my only refuge."

(2) "Even if He is a lowly person or is devoted to me, even if He destroys me with His gaze or is merciful to me, even if He does as He pleases, He is my only Lord, and there is no one else like Him."

(Siksha Sastak 8)

The one who sees the Lord's attributes, influence, and other attributes, and is devoted to them, can attain liberation, wealth, and other benefits. However, the one who is devoted to the Lord, and does not see His attributes, influence, and other attributes, can attain the Lord Himself. Not only can he attain the Lord, but he can also bind the Lord and sell Him! The Lord sees that the person is devoted to Him, and not to His attributes, influence, and other attributes, and therefore, the Lord has great respect for that person. The Lord's attributes, influence, and other attributes are like a beautiful woman, and the Lord Himself is like a lowly person. If someone sees the beautiful woman and is devoted to her, then they will attain liberation, wealth, and other benefits. However, if someone sees the lowly person and is devoted to him, then they will attain the lowly person Himself, and not the beautiful woman. The poet Surdas has said:

"If someone sees the Lord's attributes, influence, and other attributes, and is devoted to them, then they will attain liberation, wealth, and other benefits. However, if someone sees the Lord Himself, and is devoted to Him, then they will attain the Lord Himself, and not the attributes, influence, and other attributes."

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

[ Chapter 18 ]

Some people have a desire to see something. When that desire arises in our mind, we do not even notice that our body is sick. We have a sense of reverence for material things. As long as our mind has a desire, we see the effects of that desire. If our mind does not have any desire, then we will not see the effects of God's power or wealth. We will only see God's power. Then we will take refuge in God, and we will become His own. The demon Pootana had put poison in her breast milk, but God gave her the status of a mother. That is, she got the same liberation that Yashoda Maiya got. The one who gives poison in the mouth, God gave her liberation. Now, what can God give to the mother who feeds milk every day? Therefore, God has become subservient to the mother, and He has given Himself to her. The mother has become so subservient that when she shows her stick, they start crying in fear. The reason is that the mother does not have a sense of God's power or wealth. In this way, God gives liberation to those who want liberation, and He gives Himself to those who do not want anything. The secret of taking refuge in God from all aspects is that our body is good, our senses are under control, our mind is pure and clean, we have knowledge through our intellect, we are educated, we are famous, we have respect in the world - thinking like this, taking refuge in God is not devotion. After taking refuge in God, one should not think that our body should be like this, our intellect should be like this, our mind should be like this, our attention should be like this, we should have such feelings, we should have such characteristics, we should have such behavior, we should have such love that we should cry when we hear the stories of God, our throat should become hoarse - if we do not have these things in our life, then how can we take refuge in God? And so on. These things are not the criteria for true devotion. One who is devoted to God does not see God's qualities or his own qualities. He does not see the qualities of those who are dear to God, such as those who have knowledge of the truth and are liberated. Usually, people make such criteria that if someone is a devotee of God, then how can he be sick? If someone is a devotee of God, then why did he get a fever? Why did he suffer? Why did his son die? Why did his wealth go away? Why did he lose respect in the world? [ Verse 23 ]

(1) "Ah, this wicked Pootana, who put the deadly poison on her breast, even she got the right path, which is suitable for the Lord. Then, who else is merciful, to whom can I take refuge?"

(Shrimad Bhagavat 3.2.23)

(2) "Pootana went to kill, put poison on her breast. The merciful Lord gave her the status of a mother." (Vinay Patraka 214.2)

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

What a futile thing is to blame! This has made me impure, just like that. He sat there, watching, waiting for her to come. When that prostitute returned, the Maulvi scolded her, saying, "What a shameless woman you are! We were engaged in the worship of the Almighty, reciting the Quran, and you placed your feet on us! " Then she said, "I did not know you, O wise one. I read the Quran and did not know mercy."

What can be said to such people? They do not even come near to the company of the righteous. Therefore, they do not know what devotion is, what surrender is. They cannot even understand these things. But this does not mean that a devotee of the Lord is always poor, that he is always humiliated in the world, that he is always criticized. The devotee of the Lord is not concerned with praise or criticism, with health or illness, and so on. He does not even look in that direction. He only sees that he is and the Lord is, that's all. Now, what is in the world, what is not in the world, what is in the three worlds, what is not in the three worlds - the Lord is like that. He is the creator, preserver, and destroyer - He is like that. His devotee does not even look in that direction. Someone asked a saint, "Which Lord's devotee are you? One who creates, preserves, and destroys - is that a devotee of such a Lord?" The saint replied, "Our Lord has no connection with creation, preservation, and destruction. This is just one of His glories. This is not a special thing."

A devotee of the Lord should be like that. He should not even look at the glories of the Lord. In Rishikesh, near the Ganges, a group of people were engaged in a discussion. It was hot. A cool breeze from the Ganges came, and one of them said, "What a cool breeze is coming!" The person sitting next to him said, "How did you find time to look at the breeze? This cool breeze has come, this hot breeze has come - why are you so distracted?" If one is engaged in the worship of the Lord, then whether the breeze is cool or hot, whether happiness or sorrow comes - one should not even think about it. One should only think about the Lord. We have heard a story about this. The story is below, but its conclusion is very good. A person was in a state of meditation. I did not even notice that there was a wall in front of me or a person. But you were in a state of meditation, thinking about the Lord, so you noticed me. You have become a fool by reading the Quran all the time. If you were in a state of meditation, thinking about the Lord, then would you have noticed me? Who came, how did they come, was it a human or an animal - you were so distracted that you did not even notice. You were only thinking about the Lord. What is the meaning of this? One should not even think about anything except the Lord. In the past, when the Kauravas and Pandavas were children, they were learning about weapons. After learning, they were tested. A fake bird was placed on a tree, and they were asked to shoot an arrow at its throat. One by one, they came forward. The teacher first asked each of them, "What do you see there?" One said, "I see the tree," another said, "I see the branch," another said, "I see the bird, its beak, and its wings." Those who said this were sent away. When it was Arjuna's turn, he was asked, "What do you see?" Arjuna replied, "I only see the throat, and nothing else." Then he was asked to shoot the arrow, and he did. He was able to hit the bird's throat because his focus was correct. If one sees the tree, the branch, the bird, and so on, then where is the focus? The focus is only on the target. When the focus is on the target, then only the target is seen, and nothing else. This is the story of a prostitute. She received a signal from a man that she should go to a certain place at a certain time. On her way, she passed by a mosque. The Maulvi was sitting there, praying. The prostitute, unaware of this, placed her feet on him and left. The Maulvi was very angry, saying, "What kind of woman is this?" When a person's focus is not on one thing, then he does not even notice what is in front of him.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]
How can one be ananya (unattached)? The 'ananyayoga' (unattached yoga) is to be achieved. It is not easy to meet the Lord in the midst of worldly attachments! There, even the cloth gets in the way. Not just the cloth, but even the rosary can get in the way if it is placed in front of it. So, it is essential to have no companion and no material possessions with you; then the meeting with the Lord will be extraordinary and divine. One should have - 'mayi channanyayogena bhaktir avyabhicarini' (Gita 13.10). 'Ananyayoga' means that there should be no assistance from the body, mind, intellect, and ego. Only the Lord should be there. Goswami Tulsidasji Maharaj was told by someone - 'You, who worship the Lord Rama, are the twelve incarnations of the Lord, but Surdasji, who worships Lord Krishna, is the sixteen incarnations of the Lord.' Hearing this, Goswami Tulsidasji Maharaj fell at his feet and said - 'Oh! You have shown me great mercy! I was worshipping Rama as the son of Dasharathji, the king. Now I have come to know that He is the twelve incarnations of the Lord! He is so great! You have done a great favor by telling me this new thing.'

Now, Krishna is the sixteen incarnations of the Lord - this fact has not been heard by Him, and He is not even aware of it. The devotees have different feelings towards the Lord. Some say that the Lord Rama, who played in the lap of Dasharathji, is our ideal - 'Ishwara mama balaka Rama' (Mansa 7.75.3). They do not consider Raghavendraji, the king of kings, but the little Rama. Some devotees say that our ideal is the Gopala, the son of Nanda, the sweetmeat seller. They take their Rama or Gopala to the saints for blessings, and the Lord is very pleased with this. The meaning is that the devotees' vision does not go towards the Lord's majesty, but towards His love. Or, the liberation is obtained from the quality of sattva, through the love of the Gopis, who are the servants of the Lord. The Gopis are the ones who clean the path for the Lord. In the courtyard, the one where Kanhaiya plays, if someone takes that soil, then they will get four kinds of liberation. But Yashoda Maiya throws that soil out, saying it is dirt. For Maiya, it is just dirt. Now, who needs liberation? Maiya's vision is only towards Kanhaiya, not towards His majesty or His qualities. The saints have said that if one wants to meet the Lord, then one should not have a companion and no material possessions with them. If a companion and material possessions are with you, then how can you meet the Lord? The body, mind, intellect, and ego will all be obstacles. A cowherd from Vrindavan met a saint who was working in the field. The saint was a devotee of the Lord. The saint asked him - 'What do you do?' He replied - 'We work for our Lord Kanhaiya.' The saint asked - 'We are the exclusive devotees of the Lord. What are you?' He replied - 'We are the non-exclusive devotees.' The saint asked - 'What is a non-exclusive devotee?' He asked in return - 'What is an exclusive devotee?' The saint replied - 'An exclusive devotee is one who does not consider anyone else, including the sun, the goddess, Ganesha, Brahma, etc., but only our Kanhaiya.' He replied - 'Baba, we do not even know the names of these sasur (ancestors), whether they exist or not. We do not know anything about them. So, have we become non-exclusive devotees or not?'

In this way, one should not be concerned with the questions of what Brahma is, what the soul is, what is saguna and nirguna, what is sakaar and nirakaar, etc. The vision of a devotee should not go towards these things. A woman from Vrindavan came to fill water and overheard the saint talking about Brahma, the Supreme Being, the individual soul, etc. When she met another woman, she asked - 'Sakhi, what is Brahma?' The other woman replied - 'Our Lord Kanhaiya must be some relative, some neighbor, some close relative. We do not know anything about Brahma. These people are just following the path of Brahma. We have only one Nanda's son, and that is our Lord. If we need something, we will ask Nanda Baba or Giriraj. Kanhaiya is so innocent, he will not understand or do anything. What will we get from Kanhaiya? We are also alone, and Kanhaiya is also alone. We have no material possessions, and Kanhaiya has no material possessions either. He is just a naked boy - 'Nagnamurti balagupalaki, katarni barani jagjalaki.' What will we get from such a Kanhaiya?

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

The path of the one who is fearless, even in the midst of fearful circumstances, is not to be followed. Even if he is as dark as a blue sapphire, with his hands outstretched and his navel shining like a blue gem, 
do not approach him. Yashoda Maiya says to Dauji, "Look, Dauji! This Kanhaiya is very innocent and naive. Please keep an eye on him so that he doesn't wander off into the jungle." 
Dauji replies, "Mother, Kanhaiya is very restless. If he sees a snake's hole in the jungle, he'll stick his hand in it. What if the snake bites him?"

Mother Maiya says, "Beta, he's still a small child, innocent and unaware. You're older, so keep an eye on him." 
Now, Dauji and the other cowherds keep a close eye on Kanhaiya. If someone says, "Kanhaiya is the one who takes care of the whole world," 
they'll say, "You must be joking! Our Kanhaiya can't take care of the world."

A certain saint was talking to the gopis. He said, "Kanhaiya is so wealthy, his charm is so captivating, and he has such a vast treasure of wealth." 
The gopis replied, "Maharaj, the key to that treasure is in our possession. Kanhaiya has nothing, and if someone asks him for something, what can he give?"

So, if someone needs something, they shouldn't go to Kanhaiya. Only those who don't need anything should go to Kanhaiya, who is in a state of complete detachment. No one should have any desire for anything, not even in times of distress or death. If someone says, "Please help me, please protect me," 
that's not detachment; that's attachment. Lord Rama says to Valmiki, "One who never desires anything from you, 
who is always attached to you, his mind is always in your home." 
If one has no desires, then the Lord is naturally dear and sweet. The place where there are no desires is the Lord's special home. If one has desires and tries to be attached to the Lord, 
then it's not the Lord's special home. The Lord's special home is where there are no desires. The gopis warn the travelers, "Don't go that way, it's very frightening. There's a naked, dark-skinned boy standing there, his navel shining like a blue gem. He's a thief who will rob you of your thoughts, leaving you empty and helpless." 
He's a thief who will rob you of your thoughts, leaving you empty and helpless. If you go that way, you'll be ruined forever. So, if you want to live a good life, don't go that way. The one who is called Narayan is like a drunkard, 
he's lost his senses, and he's not doing anything useful. He's been captivated by the beauty of Radha. The one who has no desires, the one who is not attached to anything, 
he is the one who is always engaged in the Lord's service. He doesn't need to make an effort to serve the Lord; 
the Lord's name is naturally sweet and dear to him. If someone asks, "Why do you breathe?" 
this is not a business; this is a necessity. We can't live without breathing. Similarly, the devotee who has surrendered to the Lord can't live without serving the Lord. He's always in a state of great anxiety and restlessness, 
his mind is always preoccupied with the Lord. This is described in the Naraad Bhakti Sutra, "He becomes extremely anxious and restless when he forgets the Lord." 
If someone tells him, "If you forget the Lord for a moment, you'll get the kingdom of the three worlds," 
he'll reject this offer.

The Bhagavatam says -
For the sake of the wealth of the three worlds, even the gods and the great sages cannot forget the lotus feet of the Lord, which cannot be abandoned even for a half-moment. * Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

He who is able to abandon even the sight of the Lord's lotus feet for a half-moment is a superior devotee of Vishnu. There is no supreme being, nor the throne of Indra, nor the sovereignty of the entire earth, nor the sovereignty of the underworld, nor all the yogic perfections, nor liberation. The Lord says, 'My devotee who surrenders his self to me, I do not let go of him. He does not desire the throne of Brahma, the throne of Indra, the sovereignty of the entire earth, the sovereignty of the underworld, all yogic perfections, or liberation.'

Bharatji says -
I do not desire any worldly pleasure, nor any worldly attachment, nor any worldly activity. I do not desire any worldly wealth, nor any worldly fame. I do not desire any worldly happiness. I do not desire any worldly liberation. I am devoted to the lotus feet of Rama in this birth and in birth after birth. This is my boon. He does not desire universal sovereignty, nor the lordship of the senses. Parishishta Bhaav - The relationship of the karma yogi with the Lord is 'nitya' (eternal), the relationship of the jnana yogi is 'tattvika' (related to the ultimate truth), and the relationship of the devotee who has taken shelter is 'aatmiya' (related to the self). In the 'nitya' relationship, there is a renunciation of worldly relationships, in the 'tattvika' relationship, there is a unity with the ultimate truth (realization of the ultimate truth), and in the 'aatmiya' relationship, there is a unity with the Lord (love). In the 'nitya' relationship, there is a calm mind, in the 'tattvika' relationship, there is an unbroken mind, and in the 'aatmiya' relationship, there is a continuous mind. The hunger of the jiva is not satiated without the attainment of a continuous mind. The attainment of a continuous mind is through taking shelter. Therefore, taking shelter is the most confidential and the best means. In the phrase 'sarva-dharmaan parityajya', the meaning is not 'renunciation of all duties' but 'renunciation of the shelter of all duties'. The meaning is that there should be no reliance on any duty (karm). Just as in the first chapter, it is said - 't i me avasthitaa yuddhe praaNaans tyaktvaa dhaanaan cha' (1.33). There, 'praaNaans tyaktvaa' does not mean 'renunciation of life' but 'renunciation of the shelter of life'. Because, if one renounces life, how can one stand in the battle? It is an impossible thing. Similarly, in the ninth shloka of the first chapter, it is said - 'anye cha bahavah shooraa madaarthate tyaktajeevitaah' (1.9). Its meaning is not that many other brave warriors have renounced their lives, but that they have renounced the shelter of their lives, i.e., they do not care about their lives. Therefore, in this phrase 'sarva-dharmaan parityajya', the meaning is 'renunciation of the shelter of all duties'. Just as the brave warriors do not care about their lives, similarly, the devotee does not care about other duties. In his vision, the importance of other duties is not there. Because, the importance of taking shelter with the Lord is more than the importance of other duties. The relationship of the devotee with the Lord is related to the self, and the relationship of the duties with the self is related to the body. Therefore, the devotee does not care about other duties. The meaning of 'maam ekam sharanam vraja' is - even while showing love and respect to all in the world, one should not have any attachment to anyone, nor should one have any reliance on anyone, but one should have only the reliance on the Lord. This is the prayer of Raghuvir Goswami. And the faith - faith is the trust, the reliance on the Lord. One faith, one strength, one trust. One Rama, one Sita, one Lakshman, one Hanuman, one Tulsidas. (Vinay Patra 103)
(Dohaavali 277)

Actually, the complete surrender to the Lord is given by the Lord Himself. Just as a small child raises his hand high and the mother lifts him up, similarly, the devotee stands before the Lord with his strength, makes preparations for surrender, and the Lord gives him the complete surrender.

[Verse 67]
The seeker Arjuna desired to be freed from sins, and therefore, Lord Krishna also spoke about liberation from sins, as the Lord's nature is to treat others the way they approach Him, as stated in the verse "ye yatha mam prapadyante tams tathaiva bhajamy aham" (Gita 4.11). In reality, liberation from sins is not the only fruit of surrender. Through exclusive surrender, a person can attain oneness with the Lord and experience infinite bliss. Therefore, the seeker should not desire liberation from sins or sorrows but should simply surrender to the Lord. When one desires something, they get only that, but when one desires nothing, they get everything. The Lord also becomes bound by the devotion of the surrendered devotee and becomes indebted to them. This surrender is the essence of the Gita, which the Lord has spoken out of special grace. The completeness of the Gita's teachings lies in this surrender. Without it, the Gita remains incomplete. Therefore, after Arjuna accepted complete surrender by saying "karishye vachanam tava," the Lord did not speak further. Connection - Now, the Lord prohibits speaking the extremely confidential verse spoken earlier to those who are unqualified. Idam te na atapskaya na abhaktaya kadacana, na casushrusuve vacyam na ca mam yo 'bhyasuyati. = Thus, it should not be spoken to one who is not an ascetic, not a devotee, not one who is eager to listen, and not one who finds fault in Me. - One who is not an ascetic, one who is not a devotee, one who does not want to listen, and one who finds fault in Me, should not be spoken to. - The one who does not want to listen, 
- 'Dvandvair vimuktah sukha-duhkha-sanjñaih' (Gita 15.5). Explanation - 'Idam te na atapskaya' - The confidential verse spoken earlier, "te dvandva-mohana-nirmuktah" (Gita 7.28), "sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam sharanam vraja" - this most confidential verse is referred to by the word 'idam' here. The natural hardships that come while performing one's duty, the adverse circumstances that arise, should be endured with pleasure, and this endurance is called 'tap' (austerity). Without austerity, the heart does not become pure, and without purity, good things cannot be grasped. Therefore, the Lord says that one who is not an ascetic should not be spoken to about this most confidential secret. One who is not tolerant, i.e., one who is not patient, is also considered an ascetic. Therefore, such a person should also not be spoken to about this most confidential secret. This tolerance is of four types:
(1) Tolerance of duality - pleasure and pain, joy and sorrow, happiness and unhappiness. (2) Tolerance of impulses - not allowing impulses like lust, anger, greed, and hatred to arise - 'kama-krodha-udbhavam vegam' (Gita 5.23). (3) Tolerance of others' opinions - not doubting one's own opinion upon hearing the glory of others' opinions and not being disturbed by them - 'ekam sankhyam ca yogam ca yah pasyati sa pasyati' (Gita 5.5). (4) Tolerance of others' superiority - even if one has less capability, authority, position, renunciation, or austerity, one should not be disturbed upon hearing about others' capabilities, authority, etc. - 'vimatsarah' (Gita 4.22); one who is free from the dualities of pleasure and pain, and is not swayed by emotions like joy, anger, fear, and anxiety - 'harshamarsa-bhayodvegair muktah' (Gita 12.15). * Having differences in opinion and following one's own path is not a fault, but rather, finding fault in others' opinions, criticizing them, and having hatred towards them is a fault.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]
These four types of tolerance are of the Siddhas. These tolerances are to be narrated; because if one is forced to listen without interest, he will reject this matter, it will not be good for him to listen, his mind will reject this matter. This will also be a sin on his part. A person who commits a sin is not good. Therefore, do not listen to one who does not want to listen. One who has a goal is a tapasvi, and one who does not have a goal is an atapasi. Such an atapasi, i.e., one who is intolerant, should not be told the most confidential secret, i.e., "Surrender to Me completely, and you will be free from all sins, do not worry." If a person's mind is filled with a contrary emotion or a fault after hearing this, he will not be able to tolerate this most confidential matter and will disrespect it, which will lead to his downfall. The second aspect is that one who does not have the intention to purify his own nature, behavior, and emotions, if he hears, "If you surrender to Me, I will free you from all sins, do not worry," he will think, "I do not have to worry, God will take care of it," and will become involved in bad qualities and bad behavior, and will harm himself. This will be an improper use of My most confidential matter. Therefore, do not tell this to one who is of bad character. "Do not tell this to one who is devoid of devotion" - one who does not have devotion to God, one who does not have faith in God, one should not tell this to him; because if he does not have faith and devotion, he may think, "God is self-conceited, self-interested, and wants to control others. If one who wants to control others is God, then what benefit will I get by surrendering to Him?" and will become involved in bad qualities and bad behavior, and will suffer a great downfall. Therefore, do not tell this to one who is devoid of devotion. "Do not tell this to one who does not listen with humility" - one who does not listen with humility, one who is proud and does not listen, one should not tell this to him; because if he does not listen with humility, he will think, "God is self-conceited, self-interested, and wants to control others," and will become involved in bad qualities and bad behavior, and will suffer a great downfall. "Do not tell this to one who criticizes the good" - one who criticizes the good qualities of others, one should not tell this to him; because if he criticizes the good, his heart will be very impure, and he will criticize God's words, and will suffer a great downfall. Criticizing the good is a very great sin. This sin is also present in devotees. Therefore, the seeker should be careful and avoid this terrible sin. God Himself has said in the Gita (3.31), "The one who has faith and is not critical is liberated." In the Gita (18.71), He has said, "The one who has faith and is not critical goes to the Vaikuntha and other heavens just by listening to the Gita."

The meaning of this confidential matter is not that one should not tell others about it, but that one should not tell it to one who does not have faith and devotion to God, and who criticizes God's words. One should not tell this to one who is devoid of devotion and criticizes God's words, so that he may not think that God is self-conceited and self-interested, and may not suffer a great downfall. Commentary: God has given special importance to not telling the confidential matter to one who is devoid of devotion and one who criticizes the good. The sin of telling this to one who is devoid of devotion and one who criticizes the good is greater than telling it to one who is intolerant and one who does not want to listen. This is because one who is devoid of devotion and one who criticizes the good has a contrary mindset. "Abhakt" means one who is opposed to devotion. One who lacks devotion is not called "abhakt" here. Even a devotee may have a lack of understanding and criticism, but due to devotion, this criticism is automatically removed. The meaning of "ashushrushi" is one who does not listen due to pride. One who does not listen due to lack of understanding is not called "ashushrushi" here. 1. There is a slight difference between intolerance and criticism. Not tolerating someone's special qualities is intolerance, and criticizing someone's good qualities is criticism. 2. Even if one has faith, criticism can still be present along with it. That is why God has also said, "The one who has faith and is not critical is liberated" (Gita 3.31), and "The one who has faith and is not critical goes to the Vaikuntha and other heavens just by listening to the Gita" (Gita 18.71).

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

Do not consider the purpose of creating a sect or a group, but rather walk according to the Gita with the intention of self-improvement. The Gita advises those who are devoted to the Lord to follow its teachings, which will provide them with the means to progress on the path of self-realization, dispel their doubts, and remove the obstacles on the path. Verse 70

He who studies this sacred dialogue between us two will be dear to Me, for I consider him to be a true devotee, one who has performed the sacrifice of knowledge. Commentary:
This dialogue between the Lord and Arjuna is a rare and extraordinary opportunity. As long as a person is not disenchanted with the world, does not have a strong desire to renounce the world, and does not have a strong sense of detachment, their true inquiry is not awakened. When a person becomes anxious to decide on their duty, when they are not satisfied with any path, and when they are troubled by doubts, they become eager to find a solution. They open their heart and ask questions, pray, and take refuge. As their eagerness increases, the person who is answering their questions becomes more and more creative in providing solutions. Just as a calf sucks milk from its mother's udder, a person who is eager to learn will ask questions and receive answers that will satisfy their doubts.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]
When a seeker, driven by strong curiosity, repeatedly asks questions, 
he becomes the embodiment of the Gita, and the speaker's mind generates new answers. As the listener receives new information, their desire to listen grows. Only then does the conversation between the speaker and the listener become meaningful. 7
Arjuna had never asked such questions before, nor had the Lord ever thought of speaking such words. However, when Arjuna began to ask questions with curiosity, starting from "shtitaprajnasya ka bhasha..." (2.54), 
their conversation began to take the form of a question-and-answer dialogue from there. This contains the essence of the Vedas and Upanishads, as well as the Lord's true feelings, 
which, if one holds onto, one can easily achieve the goal of human life even in the most adverse circumstances. When adverse circumstances arise, do not be afraid; instead, respect the adversity and use it to your advantage, 
i.e., give up the desire for comfort; because adversity comes to destroy the effects of past sins 
and to make one give up the desire for comfort. The more one gives up the desire for comfort, the more one will be free from the attachment to comfort and the fear of adversity. When one is free from attachment and fear, one attains equanimity, which is the very form of the Supreme Consciousness. The Gita emphasizes the importance of equanimity, and it is called yoga in the Gita. In this way, the Gita describes the unique aspects of karma yoga, jnana yoga, bhakti yoga, dhyana yoga, pranayama, etc. The meaning of "adhyesyate" is that as one reads, recites, remembers, and tries to understand the conversation, 
their heart will become more eager. As one understands more, their doubts will be resolved. As doubts are resolved, one will become more interested. As one becomes more interested, 
their deeper feelings will be revealed in their understanding, and those feelings will manifest in their behavior, actions, and behavior. Their life will become like the Gita, and they will become a living embodiment of the Gita. People will remember the Gita when they see them, just as people remember Lakshman when they see Guha. -
,
'Jnana-yajnena tena aham istah syam' - There are two types of yajnas: dravya-yajna and jnana-yajna. The yajna that is performed with the use of material objects and actions is called dravya-yajna, 
and the yajna that is performed with the sole intention of knowing one's true nature is called jnana-yajna. However, here the Lord says that if someone reads the conversation between Arjuna and himself, 
he will be worshiped by that person as if he were performing a jnana-yajna. The reason for this is that just as a devotee becomes happy when someone speaks about their beloved, 
in the same way, someone who reads the Gita or practices it will make the Lord happy, and the Lord will be worshiped by that person. The reason for this is that when someone reads or practices the Gita, their heart will be filled with the Lord's love, 
and their mind will be filled with the Lord's presence. -
'iti me matih' - The meaning of this is that when someone reads the Gita, 
I listen to them, because I am present everywhere, and I have ears everywhere. Therefore, as soon as they read the Gita, my heart will be filled with knowledge, love, compassion, etc., 
and my mind will be filled with the memory of the Gita's speaker. They will not be performing a ritualistic worship, but they will be worshiping me, 
and they will receive the fruit of jnana-yajna. * Jani Lakhan sam dehin asisa. Jiahu sukhi say lakh barisa. Nirakhin Nishad nagar nar nar. Bhae sukhi janu Lakhanu nihari. (Mansa 2.196.3)

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

The one who studies the Gita but does not delve into its depths, merely reads it or remembers it, still, a sweet and sweet memory of our conversations and all our discussions that I have given with great depth and sincerity, starts to arise in my heart. In this way, the one who studies the Gita is doing a great service to me, I consider this to be so. The second point is that the one who reads the Gita, if he were to speak with such depth, then he would speak with such gravity, as if he were understanding the meaning, that all the members present would jump up from their seats. The members were so pleased that as soon as the lecture was over, they started throwing money. Now, that boy was being lifted up high in the assembly, everyone was lifting him on their shoulders. But that boy had no idea what I had said! He was in a party in a foreign land. There were many people there, not very educated, but they were all understanding the English language. A priest was also there, but he did not understand, but all the people in the assembly understood. They brought this one boy. That boy used to act in a play, he used to study and recite the Gita, he used to do it. The priest taught that boy a very good lecture in just ten to fifteen minutes. At the same time, he also taught him to understand the meaning and the essence of the Gita. Therefore, the Lord teaches the art of lecturing and explaining the Gita in a proper way, and also the art of seeing and understanding the Gita. In the assembly, just like the boy's lecture made the president very happy, so also the members were very happy. The subject of the lecture was also very deep. The priest taught the lecture and the members were very pleased, they started honoring the boy. They made the boy stand on the table and started honoring him. The boy, who used to act in a play, stood up and started looking around with great enthusiasm, and also started talking like a priest, saying that the Gita is the knowledge-yajna, and the one who studies the Gita is being worshiped by the Lord. The boy was acting in a play, he used to say that the Gita is the knowledge-yajna, and the one who studies the Gita is being worshiped by the Lord. He used to say that the Gita is the knowledge-yajna, and the one who studies the Gita is being worshiped by the Lord. The Lord considers the knowledge-yajna to be superior to the material yajna - 'Shreyan dravyamayad yajnah jnanayajnah parantap' (Gita 4.33). If the Gita has such great importance, then what to say about following its teachings? Connection - If one cannot even propagate and study the Gita, then what should he do? The remedy for this is given in the next shloka. Shraddhavan anasuyah cha shrinu yaadapi yo narah |

Narah = Narah (man)
Anasuyah = Anasuyah (one who is free from malice)
Cha = Cha (and)
Shrnu yaadapi = Shrnu yaadapi (even if he listens)
Yo = Yo (he)
So'pi = So'pi (also)
Muktah = Muktah (liberated)
Shubhaan lokan = Shubhaan lokan (good worlds)
Prapnu yaat = Prapnu yaat (he will attain)
Punyakarmanam = Punyakarmanam (of pious deeds)

Even if a man with faith and free from malice listens to the Gita, he will also be liberated and attain good worlds. * Wherever the Gita is studied, there all the tirthas, including Prayag, are present. There all the gods, sages, yogis, divine serpents, Gopala, Gopikas, Narada, Uddhava, and other sages are present. *

Wherever the Gita is studied, there I, the Lord, reside forever.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
The meaning of the term 'shradhavananasuyashca' is that one who believes in the words of the Gita as it is, without any doubt or criticism, is called a 'shradhavanan' (one who has faith), and one who does not see any fault or imperfection in the words of the Gita is called an 'anasuy' (one who is free from criticism). If such a person, who is free from criticism and has faith, listens to the Gita, even if he does not understand it, he will be liberated from all sins and will attain the heavenly realms of the virtuous. [ Chapter 18
A devotee of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu complained to him that 'see, the Lord is a hypocrite; he does not purify the path and cries all the time.' Chaitanya Mahaprabhu called him to his side and asked, 'Do you understand the meaning of the Gita?' He replied, 'No, Lord!' Then he asked, 'So why do you cry?' He said, 'When I read 'Arjuna uvacha', it seems to me that Arjuna is asking questions to the Lord, and when I read 'Shri Bhagavan uvacha', it seems to me that the Lord is answering Arjuna's questions. In this way, it seems to me that the Lord and Arjuna are having a conversation with each other. But I do not understand what Arjuna is asking and what the Lord is answering.' He said, 'I am satisfied just by seeing the Lord and Arjuna.' Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was very pleased with his devotion and faith. If a person like this, who has faith and devotion, listens to the Gita, there is no doubt that he will be liberated. He will be free from all sins and will attain the heavenly realms of the virtuous. The phrase 'api' is used twice to emphasize that one who propagates the Gita, studies it, and has faith in it is indeed liberated. But even one who listens to it is also liberated from all sins and attains the heavenly realms. A person's speech is often affected by four defects: doubt, carelessness, desire, and lack of skill. Therefore, a person's speech is never completely free from defects. However, the divine speech of the Lord is free from all these defects, because the Lord is beyond all defects. Therefore, there is no possibility of doubt or criticism in the words of the Lord. Therefore, if one does not understand a particular topic or concept, one should not doubt the Gita. Instead, one should think that one's own understanding is limited, and one should have faith in the Gita. If one has faith in the Gita, even if one does not understand it, one will be free from criticism and will attain the heavenly realms. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu had a devotee who used to read the Gita every day. He would become ecstatic and cry, but he did not read the Gita properly. His reading was full of mistakes. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's devotees were concerned about this. Parishishta Bhaav:
The phrase 'shubhaanllokaan praptunyata punyakarmaanam' means that one who has faith and devotion will attain the heavenly realms, and the more faith and devotion one has, the higher one will attain. The heavenly realms range from the material world to the realm of the Lord. If one has more faith and devotion, one will attain the realm of the Lord, and if one has less faith and devotion, one will attain the material world. The merit of keeping the Gita is great. Even if one does not study or listen to the Gita, just keeping it is beneficial. A soldier once said that the Gita is like a sword that can cut through all doubts and criticisms. He said that the speaker of the Gita should be free from doubt, carelessness, desire, and lack of skill. If the speaker is free from these defects, the Gita will be beneficial. The four defects that affect a speaker are:

(1) Bhram (doubt): the speaker should not be doubtful about the topic he is speaking about. (2) Pramad (carelessness): the speaker should not be careless about the topic he is speaking about. (3) Lipsha (desire): the speaker should not be motivated by desire or personal gain. (4) Karanaapata (lack of skill): the speaker should not lack the skill or ability to communicate effectively.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

He was returning home at night from somewhere. On the way, he saw a beautiful woman under the light of the moon in the shade of a tree. He talked to her and she said, "May I come in?" The soldier said, "Yes, come in." After the soldier said this, the woman, who was actually a witch, followed him. Now, every night, she would come to the soldier's place, sleep with him, and leave in the morning. In this way, she began to exploit the soldier, sucking his blood and weakening his strength. One night, they both lay down, but the light remained on. The soldier told her to turn off the light. She lay down and, without getting up, stretched her hand to turn off the light. Now, the soldier realized that she was no ordinary woman, but a witch! He was very frightened. The witch threatened him, saying, "If you tell anyone about me, I will kill you." In this way, she would come to his place every night and leave in the morning. The soldier's body was becoming weaker day by day. People would ask him, "Brother, why are you becoming so weak? What's the matter? Tell us!" But, out of fear of the witch, he wouldn't tell anyone anything. One day, he went to the shop to buy medicine. The shopkeeper gave him a packet of medicine, which he put in his pocket and went home. When the witch came that night, she stood at a distance and said, "Take out the packet from your pocket and throw it away." The soldier thought that there must be some magic in the packet, which is why the witch wasn't coming to him anymore. He told her, "I won't throw it away." The witch begged him, but he didn't listen to her. When the witch realized she couldn't control him, she left. The soldier took out the packet from his pocket and saw that it was a torn page from the Gita! In this way, he realized the power of the Gita and started carrying it with him always. Connection - In the previous shloka, the glory of listening to the Gita was described. Now, Lord Krishna asks Arjuna, "What is your situation, what is your state, etc.?" knowing everything about Arjuna's situation, yet with the intention of revealing the glory of listening to the Gita to everyone, he asks Arjuna in the next shloka. Mind

Has Arjuna, with a single-minded mind, heard even a little bit of this? Has the ignorance-induced delusion been destroyed in you, O Partha? Arjuna

O son of Pritha! Has Arjuna, with a single-minded mind, heard even a little bit of this? Explanation - 'Kachchid etachchrutam parth tvayekagreN chetasaa' - 'Etat' is a very close relative word and here it refers to the previous shloka, which is the 131st shloka. In the previous 70 shlokas, the glory of listening to the Gita and its study has been described. Arjuna had no question about this. Therefore, Lord Krishna, looking at the 131st shloka, asks Arjuna, "Has Arjuna, with a single-minded mind, heard even a little bit of this?" i.e., "Has Arjuna listened to the Gita with faith and without any defects?"

'Kachchid ajnansam mohah pranasth te dhannjaya' - Lord Krishna asks another question, "Has the ignorance-induced delusion been destroyed in you, O Dhannjaya?" If the delusion has been destroyed, then Arjuna has listened to the Gita's mysterious teachings. If the delusion has not been destroyed, then Arjuna has not listened to the Gita's mysterious teachings with a single-minded mind.

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *
[ Chapter 18 ]

Because it is an absolute rule that when the family attachment—considered a defect of perception—awakens and one listens to the teaching of the Gita with devotion, free from that attachment, the delusion is destroyed. Addressing Arjuna as “Partha,” the Lord, with great affection, asks whether his delusion has indeed been eliminated. In Chapter 1, Verse 25 the Lord also began by addressing Arjuna as “Partha” to turn his mind toward listening, saying, “O Partha, behold these family members gathered for battle.” The purpose was to make the latent attachment in Arjuna’s heart apparent, so that he would become eager to hear the Lord directly. Here, concluding the removal of that attachment, the Lord again uses the address “Partha.”

By addressing him as “Dhananjaya,” the Lord says that Arjuna has become a conqueror of wealth (the wealth of kings). Now, by attaining the true essence of wealth, destroy your delusion and become a genuine “Dhananjaya” in the fullest sense. **Relation** – In the preceding verse the Lord posed a question; Arjuna answers it in the following verse. **Arjuna said**  
[ Verse 73 ]  
nasto mohaḥ smṛtiḥ labdhā tvat‑prasādān mayā‑acyuta |  
sthito ’smi gata‑sandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṁ tava ||

*Word‑by‑word breakdown*  
nasto‑mohaḥ: delusion destroyed  
smṛtiḥ‑labdhā: memory obtained  
tvat‑prasādāt: by your grace  
mayā‑acyuta: O Achyuta, by me (address)  
sthito ’smi: I am established, steady  
gata‑sandehaḥ: free from doubt  
kariṣye‑vacanaṁ‑tava: I will carry out your command

**Explanation** – The declaration “nasto mohaḥ smṛtiḥ labdhā tvat‑prasādāt – I will obey your command” does not affect the Lord. It implies that Arjuna experiences three phases—beginning, middle, and end—whereas the Lord remains unchanged in all three, ever the same. In Chapter 2, Verse 7 Arjuna had said “śiṣyaste ’ham śādhī māṁ tvāṁ prapannam,” accepting complete surrender to the Lord; this verse expresses the fullness of that surrender. The address “mayā‑acyuta” (Achyuta) is used here for the Lord. It signifies that the individual soul may become “chyuta” (deviated from its true nature) and head toward decline, whereas the Lord never becomes “chyuta”; He remains ever immutable. To illustrate this, Arjuna employs the address “Achyuta” three times in the Gita:

1. Chapter 1, Verse 21 – Arjuna asks the Lord to place his chariot between the two armies. 2. Chapter 11, Verse 42 – Arjuna praises the Lord’s universal form. 3. Here, Chapter 18, Verse 73 – free from doubt, Arjuna declares that his delusion has vanished: “moho’ayam vigato mama” (Verse 11.1, “this delusion of mine is gone”). At the end of Chapter 10 the Lord told Arjuna that there is no need for him to know everything, for the Lord pervades the entire universe in a single fragment. Hearing this, Arjuna felt a special emotion, recognizing how extraordinary the Lord is. This realization illuminated Arjuna, and with joy he exclaimed, “My …” (the passage ends).

* Srimad Bhagavad Gita *

When Arjuna's heart was filled with fear upon seeing the vast form of the Lord, the Lord said, "This is your foolishness, do not be distressed and do not be deluded" (11.49). This proves that Arjuna's delusion had not been destroyed. Now, when the all-knowing Lord asks, Arjuna says, "My delusion has been destroyed, and I have obtained the memory of the eternal truth" - "Nashto Mohah Smritirlabdhah". There is a great difference between the memory of the heart and the memory of the eternal truth. The knowledge of the means of knowledge (pramana) and the object of knowledge (prameya) is obtained through the means of knowledge, but the eternal truth (paramatma) is beyond the means of knowledge. Therefore, the eternal truth is not included in the means of knowledge. However, the world is included in the means of knowledge, and the means of knowledge is included in the knower (pramatA). The knower is one, and the means of knowledge are many. Many people consider the three main means of knowledge to be direct perception, inference, and scripture. Some consider the four means of knowledge to be direct perception, inference, analogy, and word. And some consider the three additional means of knowledge to be arthapatti (inference from the presence of something), anupalabdhi (inference from the absence of something), and itihasa (scripture). In this way, there are many differences of opinion about the means of knowledge, but there is no difference of opinion about the knower. These means of knowledge are of the nature of vritti (mental modification), but the knower is not of the nature of vritti, but is self-conscious (anubhavavritti). (1) AnubhutavishayasmpramoshaH smritiH. (Yogadarshan 1.11)
"Memory is the awareness of the unobscured object."

(2) Samskaramatrajanyam jnanam smritiH. (Tarkasangrah)
"Knowledge born of samskara (impression) is memory."

This memory is a vritti of the antahkarana (mind). This vritti is of five types: pramana (means of knowledge), viparyaya (error), vikalpa (false assumption), nidra (sleep), and smriti (memory). Each type of vritti has two sub-types: klishta (tainted) and aklishta (untainted). The vritti related to the world is klishta, i.e., binding, and the vritti related to the Lord is aklishta, i.e., liberating. The cause of all these vrittis is avidya (ignorance). However, the Lord is beyond ignorance. Therefore, the memory of the Lord is obtained directly, not through vritti or karana (instrument). When the memory of the Lord is awakened, it never forgets, whereas the memory of the antahkarana (mind) is subject to both memory and forgetfulness. The forgetfulness of the eternal truth is the cause of the world's existence and its importance. This forgetfulness has been present since time immemorial. Although it has been present since time immemorial, its end is possible. When its end comes and the memory of one's true nature is awakened, it is said to be "smritirlabdhah". Now, the explanation of the word "smriti" is given, which says that the memory that was in a state of susupti (dreamless sleep) has become awakened. Just as a person who was in a state of sleep becomes awake, similarly, the memory that was in a state of susupti has become awakened. 1. Arjuna's samsarik (worldly) and shastrik (scriptural) delusions have both been destroyed (Gita 2.42 and 2.43). 2. The knowledge of the world is obtained through direct perception, inference, etc. because the world is a subject of vivek (discrimination). However, the one who is the light of vivek (discrimination) and the refuge of all cannot be known through vivek (discrimination). This is because the one who is to be known is not capable of being known by the one who knows. Therefore, the eternal truth is a subject of shraddha (faith) and not of vivek (discrimination). Those who have shraddha (faith) in the scriptures accept the eternal truth as per the scriptures, and those who have shraddha (faith) in the saints and sages accept the eternal truth as per their words. In this case, the scriptures and the saints and sages are the means of knowledge, not the antahkarana (mind) and the senses. For those who have shraddha (faith), the scriptures and the saints and sages are the means of knowledge, but for those who do not have shraddha (faith), they are not the means of knowledge. The meaning of this is that the subject of the antahkarana (mind) and the senses is a direct perception, and the means of knowledge such as inference, etc. are indirect means of knowledge. However, the scriptures and the saints and sages are the means of knowledge based on shraddha (faith). 3. That by which one is known is called "pramana" (means of knowledge), that which is known is called "prameya" (object of knowledge), and that which knows is called "pramatA" (knower). The senses and the antahkarana (mind) are the means of knowledge, the world is the object of knowledge, and the self (chit) is the knower.
